Hello Friend,

We both know that a March snowstorm won't keep Minnesotans from dreaming of warmer days ahead. Spring is just around the corner and that means the end of the first quarter is fast-approaching. I need your help!
** March 31st marks the end of our first fundraising reporting period.

**These reports are one of the ways people measure the strength and momentum of a campaign.

**Can you help me build that momentum with a donation?
**
[Dr. Scott Jensen | Donate to Further the Cause](http://email.mg.drscottjensen.com/c/eJxMjzHO3CAQRk9jGosVDNhAQZFmj5A2GjODfyIbVoZNcvzImybtm_ek-fBNhWviH4Wi9kqDSK0OTOMDFtqy1VY6cEna7FniglluaFBvnjAACoqZApgsOGrnTADlHYivuCZr3eKTzsZtKljILltP3oLyhnMWJYKCVRkdlFJqWR5kvEuoNWtejPI8WXXuD7p6amP85Nq5PlI7xRG_xnj1yXyb4DnBs3N6X_zAytTGbdzsbuS_SOZ2ybPUyr0NnOBJreJgcXLvuH-mM60JwxKkURtIS5Zk8EnJ7HFztBLajKJd--16A7SuDmSGDNL6JUivMsg1eJ1wocybEVek1-9yHKWvbrJqP7Ecn-dH_M5XyYVp5hv2mf-k402l7jO12q4-63m02c1Y6b_b6-Lexa8IfwMAAP__rsKIKg)

Minnesota needs a State Auditor with the experience and good judgment to make sure our tax money is properly managed. For 40 years, I have held leadership roles that required me to steward large budgets and lead organizations:

* **Financial Leadership:** I led the audit committee for a billion-dollar bank for more than ten years.

* **Accounting Experience:** I served as a board member for a professional accounting firm.

* **Budget Oversight:** In the MN Senate, I was Vice Chair of the Health & Human Services Committee, which oversees one of the largest portions of our state’s budget

* **Community Service:** I presided over several local groups, including Chambers of Commerce, Lions, and Rotary Clubs.

* **Education & Schools:** I led my local school board and managed complex contract negotiations with teachers.

* **Business Owner:** As the founder and owner of several companies, I understand the value of a dollar and the need for efficient operations.

* **Data-driven Oversight: **As a doctor, I’ve spent my career studying large amounts of complicated data and medical statistics to make critical decisions for my patients. I will use this skill to look closely at our state’s spending and find the "warning signs" of government waste.

I am ready to put this experience to work for you!

Friend, I care deeply about our state and the communities we call home. Our future is at stake.

As State Auditor, I will work to protect taxpayer dollars by strengthening oversight, conducting audits to verify compliance, and proactively preventing fraud and misuse of public funds.

Right now, many Minnesotans feel that trust in government has been shaken.

Strong and independent financial oversight can help restore that trust.
If you are able, **please consider donating today to help our campaign continue growing.**
[**Dr. Scott Jensen | Donate to Further the Cause**](http://email.mg.drscottjensen.com/c/eJxMjzHO3CAQRk9jGosVDNhAQZFmj5A2GjODfyIbVoZNcvzImybtm_ek-fBNhWviH4Wi9kqDSK0OTOMDFtqy1VY6cEna7FniglluaFBvnjAACoqZApgsOGrnTADlHYivuCZr3eKTzsZtKljILltP3oLyhnMWJYKCVRkdlFJqWR5kvEuoNWtejPI8WXXuD7p6amP85Nq5PlI7xRG_xnj1yXyb4DnBs3N6X_zAytTGbdzsbuS_SOZ2ybPUyr0NnOBJreJgcXLvuH-mM60JwxKkURtIS5Zk8EnJ7HFztBLajKJd--16A7SuDmSGDNL6JUivMsg1eJ1wocybEVek1-9yHKWvbrJqP7Ecn-dH_M5XyYVp5hv2mf-k402l7jO12q4-63m02c1Y6b_b6-Lexa8IfwMAAP__rsKIKg) **The maximum contribution to the Auditor campaign is ****$2,000 per person / $4,000 per couple**
I would be honored to have your support \- any amount you can give will help us reach more voters and build momentum before the March 31 deadline.

Together, we can bring back lawful, efficient, and transparent stewardship of taxpayer dollars and help Minnesota shine again as the Star of the North.

Thank you so much!

Scott Jensen
Candidate for State Auditor

subject: They didn't even take input from county officials who actually run elections
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Integrity First Voter Action Project, www
body:
The worst part of this new law? The Ohio legislature wrote and passed this bill without any input from the officials across the state who actually run the elections.
“ It’s a solution to a non-existent problem, ” said Warren County election official Bethe Goldenfield. “ I don’t see where this is doing anything to help voters. It’s only going to disenfranchise people .”
This is all part of a partisan push to preserve their own power. RUSH $35 or more to help us fight back against these attacks on mail-in voting and more >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=031826_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Bolts: Ohio Bans Grace Periods for Mail Ballots, Fulfilling Trump’s Wishes [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=031826_3&amount=25]
Ohio has made it harder to vote by mail, Team .
Senate Bill 293, which was recently signed into law, repeals Ohio’s practice of counting mail ballots that are postmarked prior to Election Day but that arrive up to four days after polls close. Now, any ballots delayed in the mail that arrive after Election Day won't count in Ohio.
This follows executive orders from President Trump, who is against mail-in voting despite voting that way himself , and has called for ending these so-called grace periods for mail ballots everywhere. Ohio’s new law follows his lead, threatening thousands of votes in the process.
We've said it before and we'll keep saying it: Mail-in balloting is safe and secure. It's a nonpartisan way for eligible voters to make their voices heard in our elections. And now it's harder for them to participate in elections in Ohio, whether they're a military member voting from overseas, someone who is immunocompromised, in a nursing home, or any other reason for voting by mail.
Defending vote-by-mail is a crucial part of protecting our fundamental right to vote. Chip in with $35 or whatever you can today to support mail-in voting across the country >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-democracy?refcode=031826_3&amount=35]

Trump has long lied about mail-in voting. He's claimed mail-in voting contributed to his 2020 election loss, though no widespread fraud has been found. In fact, the one case of mail-in ballot fraud in Pennsylvania after the 2020 election was a man who was prosecuted for returning his dead mother's ballot for Trump .
The use of mail-in voting has become very common across the country and study after study has shown that fraud in mail-ballot voting is rare. There are also several safeguards in place nationwide to protect against fraud, including signature requirements and barcodes to track envelopes sent by officials. States have spent tens of millions of taxpayer dollars investigating voter fraud since 2020's "big lie" and found virtually nothing.
In Ohio, this new law will result in thousands of ballots being thrown out. We know this because thousands of ballots were accepted in the grace period in previous selections, some of them making the difference in local elections -- like in Warren County, where several races came down to single-digit margins.
Being blunt: There is no good-faith reason to end the vote-by-mail grace period. Just like the other Trump attacks on our elections in general and mail-in voting in particular -- this is a partisan voter suppression exercise meant to codify MAGA's power in perpetuity.

body:

Peter,

Our movement only exists because people like you stepped up when it
mattered most.

Every donation, every action, every message of support, it all adds up,
and it’s the reason the Squad is still fighting for working people today.

Alexandria, Ayanna, Ilhan, and Rashida are showing up every day – pushing
bold policies that center the communities too often ignored and fighting
for justice across the board: economic, social, racial, and healthcare.

But let’s be honest about what that kind of leadership costs.

Speaking truth to power comes with consequences. And the Squad is
constantly under attack by powerful interests who would rather silence
them than allow real, progressive change to take hold.

That means we have to be louder, stronger, and more organized than ever.
That’s where you come in.

Your support fuels the work that makes this movement real — organizing on
the ground, reaching voters directly, and building the kind of coalition
it takes to win across the country.

This is what people power looks like and how we win.

It's time to force the fight.

**It passed the House.**

President Trump is 100% behind it.

The American people want it. _It's common sense._

The only reason that the Save America Act is not law is that Republican Senators don't have the guts to fight for it.

You already know I’m against Donald Trump. Today, I want to tell you what I’m for:
I’m for democracy.

I’m for freedom of speech and religion.

name: Juliana Stratton
subject: We did it! But our fight is just beginning
body:
---
| [](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-stratton-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260318_6434_fr&refcode2=6434_22930333_YISyL0&akid=6434%2E22930333%2EYISyL0)
---
Derek,
I am humbled and honored to be your Democratic nominee for United States Senate!
Illinois sent a clear message last night: We’re ready to take our democracy back.
In the past year, we’ve seen Donald Trump wage war on working families to bankroll tax breaks for his allies, strip health care from Americans, and relentlessly terrorize our communities.
But I’ve seen the very best of Illinois respond. People who took to the streets, stood up for their neighbors, and refused to back down. Time and again, with everything on the line, Illinois showed up.
Together, we've confronted the most frightening moments of lifetimes. Despite the fear, we're all finding the courage to keep going.
Courage inspired me to run. Courage powered this campaign. And courage will bring this fight straight to Donald Trump’s door.
This campaign was built on a simple belief: We are stronger when we stand together, and we are unshakeable when we turn our fear into courage and our anger into action.
That was the mission at the outset... and that is the mission we have accomplished.
But our fight is just beginning, Derek. Today, we turn to face a Republican opponent in the general election. We will confront new challenges and new attacks from a candidate unfit to stand up to Donald Trump, uninterested in fighting for your needs, and unwilling to challenge the status quo that has failed our families.
Every day until November 3, we will be laser-focused on making sure every Illinoisan knows exactly what is at stake.
So as our work begins again, I am counting on your continued support. The only way we can win this race is if we tackle what’s next just like how we’ve tackled the last 11 months — together.
[**Can you please split $20 between the DNC and my campaign for U.S. Senate to help us get the general election off to a strong start and win in Illinois and beyond? We need to be ready for whatever our Republican opponents send our way.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-stratton-split?amount=20&refcode=em_20260318_6434_fr&refcode2=6434_22930333_YISyL0&akid=6434%2E22930333%2EYISyL0)

In this episode of The Robinson Report, host Steve sits down with former Maine Senate Republican Leader and 2026 gubernatorial candidate Garrett Mason for a wide-ranging conversation about his path to the race, his vision for the state, and the policy battles ahead. Mason discusses his entry into the U.S. Senate in 2010 and becoming Maine's youngest-ever Senate Republican Leader. He highlights his gubernatorial plans on tax reform, energy costs, housing, immigration enforcement, and education The conversation also digs into Mason's positioning within a competitive Republican primary field, his critiques of the Mills administration's record on welfare spending and asylum seeker resettlement, and his approach to governing as an experienced Augusta insider.

## Trump Opens US Ports to Foreign Tankers
President Trump issued a 60-day waiver of the Jones Act, a century-old law requiring cargo between U.S. ports to be carried on [American-built, American-owned, American-flagged, and American-crewed ships](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSgyAURb9GOxxAQS0otrHLtls6KI_4MigOD8Pm73eSX9j-zp1zzs9tvlkMeNy_7Q4m-zgfUChAzpDmnK79jCccdNEZUyZn142265gll5rxlolxdhbDa-5qZzyAhLYGI_q-HUU3qqHejOrloK3Wzo6LFkINS6uU19C3g-5AuRrN-423YhScj0I1nbLeaa9Bjc5rrquOg8McU_OIeOQNfHjFJ6RmjXsdzJbzSVX7VcmpklMppfHxd7kIDyB6byo5nTFgxpUqOX2kWLH4BGKPeAAxu2amOXP2RWxBx3wCYNfJfIiFRQzsojoZdxYMAUn3Vcfvu8XwAcj_qvY08i8AAP__KV2DmQ), in an effort to ease fuel costs as the war with Iran chokes off the Strait of Hormuz. The strait normally carries about a fifth of the world's oil, and its effective closure has pushed [Brent crude above $103 per barrel](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGOwyAUBNDT4M4RYENCQbGNu2y7JULmE_8VBgTfiXL7lXOFrUd6M5qfu7t7TJgf334HS7G4DK-egAiao3bstVTI_ei1NOrBr1vfjuwkl3rk0yiMCx7T281DsBFAwjSAFdfrZMRs1G3YrDCeg5k9yBCj0EGtwUQvbqC81kbDgPbU-CSM4NwIdZmVj0FHDcqEqLlmM4eAVNrlt2CmDWJ6lye0y1r2IdmNqHY2fTG5MLnE0ujIcGZMLr4RrgmYXGrDFcYSx4Lps_w2nrVMLkOzob4wJez6ymb-2D2mj03_OuRp5V8AAAD__-oGdGc) and sent the average U.S. gas price to $3.84 per gallon. The waiver opens domestic ports to foreign vessels carrying oil, natural gas, fertilizer, and coal, removing a bottleneck that has long driven up [shipping costs between U.S. ports](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGu4yAUAE-DOyLABpuCYht32XZL68U87BdhsIAk8u1X-Vf49Ugz0vy7L3egSGn7Cwe6FvKS8FMjtoZlaeV1nPnEVF_1zKVVD-te91dalFCGi55Lu3igeC1D511AVNh36OQ49lYOVk_d7lCbcQKlHlr2D8A--PBAmBBGK00IpiP3tYleWimElfo2aAjeBIPa-mCEYYNATy2X2zNTajuGeOU3ltuajy66vbWzsv4PUzNTc9txpxi_jKn5zJHWi6kZE5bt4pjeVHI6MDWmZj1OVuuRU4HEP1D4MyesHNbGN6j8LLRiZWruivPnh2KkakY2iO0A-il07VfL3k79DwAA__8UM4Ih). The Jones Act has been waived multiple times for emergencies, including after Hurricane Katrina in 2005, Hurricane Maria in 2017, and the Colonial Pipeline cyberattack in 2021.
## TSA Warns Some Airports Could Close
The Transportation Security Administration is warning that some airports [could shut down entirely](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO6yAYhJ8Gd464-UJBcaQjd9l2S4uYH8MKA4LfifL2K-cVtp0ZzWi-7_t6NyGGtH-ZAzS6vCZ4tQiIUFes51FygdTOVnLFZs3mmz_Tyikfeyp6plZrQnyvsrPaAXAQHWg2TUIxqYa58_oxGyY244QARRnYeZSTcVbCpjbLp6kL-mqjgilGqWLDTQ7G2dGNMCjrRjoSScEGzPX2k0NCDy6-8xPqbctHF7VHLI2If4QvhC_owYcYL4_wpeQYtvclV5M-HwyGnAhfhmmexSx7bKbPzoUNausb1nPfI_TNn2jz6woSseCjgiPivy9d1ba8QoyhjRORdD9M-Gx1-Cd4T81_AwAA__8vdYXJ) if employee sick days continue to climb during the partial government shutdown. More than 10% of TSA officers nationwide called out on March 15, five times the normal rate. Atlanta is seeing 37% of its workforce absent and wait times topping two hours. Hundreds of officers have quit, and the 50,000 still showing up are working without pay, with [some struggling to afford gas](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAYhJ9GOwz8IrsUFNfY7bVXGoSflQuKgd81-_YX9xWum2QyM_nm5zE9bExxe37bFQ2FPG141oREWCYqx7rnHbd61D0Xqt66pS7HNgEHxXjPhJ68jek9ydabgAjYt2jE7dZrIfVwbxdzvw_aKZg5eBRiCCgQeqE8SCctzLqN5mrjvdCCcy2GTg42eBUUDtoHxVUjOfpIuXS_OW60YEjv_MLSuby2ySxEe236rwbGBsbzPDs314vi8hsYL9nASNUyG8uHg7l8JM_qchDz-dxYDiE6LMzZlFg-iBVLyFyK63xl22L8fsaUYlW3RvLnamP6zNO_PnsZ-AsAAP__X5SDJw) after missing their first full paycheck last week. Three of Philadelphia's six checkpoints will be closed Wednesday, and officials say the situation will only worsen the longer Congress blocks funding for the Department of Homeland Security.
## ****Ranking: Where Americans Live Longest
New government data shows that average life expectancy [varies dramatically across states](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFyhCAUAL8GOxxAwaOgSGN3aVM67-RxkkFh5HnGv89cfiH9zu7Mft2nO8QUt-cnrOgo5GnDsyYkwn2i_VhLLrjVo5a8U_UwL3U5tkkJZbjouLSTh5iuqW-8C4gKuwadHIbOyt7qW7M4pa154KARBmsDagAwKBGGh5JC3romurdNdNJKIazUba8heBMMauuDEYb1An2kvLffOW60YEhXfuHeznltkluISmXdB1MjU-N5nu0r1gPSDCUSpFjpDTI1rlAKen5UnmJAjj8FZ4Jtvvjj4pWAkKmx2Z0vZ0wpVjOwXjxXiOmvRP_a83LqNwAA__-Ienw6), with a nearly eight-year gap between the top and bottom. The national average is 77.5 years. Hawaii boasts the longest average life span at 80 years, while West Virginia has the shortest, at 72.2 years. The Northeast and West Coast consistently rank highest, while Southern and Appalachian states trail, a pattern tied to higher rates of [obesity, diabetes, and poverty](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDFu7CAYhE-Du7UAYzAFxWvc7WtTWiz8LEQYEGBbe_tooygXSDUzzXzS93Hf7jrEkJ7_9Q6qu7wluFqE3qFuvR57yQVSO1rJtTerjW_-SBvFlN_wdCNyszrE18YGqxwAhWkARYSYJGFyXgavyLJI5oQWIOBBuBGYP7AzzMEyPzgjQ1DvNzwRSTCWZB7ZrJ3ljsMsreOYI4bBhp7r-JlD6h5cfOUT6mjyPkTley8NTf8QXRFdr-sajTXjM5-Irsn4huhqddfvdbb6E4L9lhuhY7FuqMqWK8QYGheI4eeuQ_xG9D95ORX9CgAA__-xynbB). More than half of the states fall below the national average, and women outlive men in every single state. Overall, life expectancy rose 1.1 years from 2021 to 2022, the first annual increase following two years of large declines driven largely by the COVID-19 pandemic. [See the full chart here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFyhCAUAL8GOxxAwaOgSGN3aVM67-RxkkFh5HnGv89cfiH9zu7Mft2nO8QUt-cnrOgo5GnDsyYkwn2i_VhLLrjVo5a8U_UwL3U5tkkJZbjouLSTh5iuqW-8C4gKuwadHIbOyt7qW7M4pa154KARBmsDagAwKBGGh5JC3romurdNdNJKIazUba8heBMMauuDEYb1An2kvLffOW60YEhXfuHeznltkluISmXdB1MjU-N5nu0r1gPSDCUSpFjpDTI1rlAKen5UnmJAjj8FZ4Jtvvjj4pWAkKmx2Z0vZ0wpVjOwXjxXiOmvRP_a83LqNwAA__-Ienw6).

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. | | Friend,
The first big race of 2026 for Democrats isn't a congressional or senate race, it's a Wisconsin Supreme Court seat that is up for grabs on April 7th.
Stopping Trump from stacking state Supreme Courts is paramount. These courts decide election laws and even outcomes. If MAGA captures them, Trump can rig elections, lock in one-party rule, and clear the path to a third term.
And Wisconsin isn't just any state. If MAGA wins this election, they'll have an opportunity to seize control of the court just months before the 2028 presidential election. We all know how this works: the presidency comes down to a handful of swing states. If MAGA controls Wisconsin's highest court, it could be game over for Dems.
Don't just take it from us. MAGA's WI Supreme Court candidate for the April election, Maria Lazar, shows Trump's endgame:

| MAGA's handpicked WI Supreme Court judge hopeful not only has ties to election deniers, she's touting their support.
Jim Troupis and Michael Gableman were both instrumental in pushing the "big lie" after Trump lost the 2020 election, spearheading efforts for the Trump legal team to try and overturn the election results in Wisconsin.
Troupis was also involved in the fake elector scheme for Wisconsin, which he was later indicted for on a felony charge. In November, Donald Trump issued a pardon for him.
If these are the types of people Lazar openly touts the support of, we know exactly what she would do if a decision that could sway an election in MAGA's direction landed in her lap as a WI Supreme Court judge.
Lazar must be defeated.

Wade_ a “devastating error,” praised extreme abortion bans, and repeatedly used inflammatory language about immigrants and pregnant people.
[At a time when there are already serious concerns about abuse and neglect of pregnant and postpartum people in DHS custody, putting someone like Mullin in charge would be indefensible.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/127619908/608669948/-621514421?sourceid=1151224&utm_campaign=march emails&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=mullin&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMWUzMmVkNS05MzIzLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=q032rgcURveNtmsUw9594xPQePkU2eHc7u9PXRdRIq0=&emci=5ef6dfc4-3b22-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=d1e32ed5-9323-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts.

By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina.

Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks.

She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.

Nancy is fighting to:

* Eliminate South Carolina’s Income Tax—the highest in the Southeast

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency

* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free

* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate

* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think

* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front.

South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.

clean_body: | | | | | | | | Hi, This is Brigadier General James Emory Mace, U.S. Army (Retired). Today, I write to you not as a soldier... but as a father. I’m a Vietnam War Veteran and Purple Heart Medal recipient. I’ve worn the uniform. I’ve buried friends who never made it home. And I’ve felt the sting of a Nation that sometimes forgets what our sacrifices were for. But my daughter - Congresswoman Nancy Mace - never forgot. Nancy was raised in the shadow of the flag. She saw the uniform. She lived with the deployments. She knew the cost. And instead of running from it, she ran toward it. That’s the kind of person -the kind of fighter \- she is. When Nancy was 17, she dropped out of high school. Most kids in that situation fall apart. But not Nancy. I raised her to believe that setbacks don’t define you -how you rise does. She grew up hearing the same lessons over and over again: 👉 Never quit. 👉 Never run from the truth.👉 And never let anyone tell you thatyou are less than what God made you to be. So I gave her a choice: She picked herself up, took a job at Waffle House, and fought her way back. By 21, she became the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, following in my footsteps. Soon after, she was elected as the first woman to represent South Carolina in the U.S. House of Representatives. She’s been fighting her whole life; for herself, for her kids, for the truth, and now...for her state. Nancy led an evacuation mission in the Middle East after learning a South Carolina family was stranded. Because when your people are stuck in a war zone getting hit with missiles and rockets, the only answer worthy of the office -worthy of our country \- is to get them out. She flew into an active war zone and answered the call when Americans needed help. As a father - and as a Purple Heart Veteran \- I’ve never been more proud of my daughter. That’s why it’s hard when I have to watch Nancy face relentless attacks day after day. Each day that goes out there and fights for you, she’s up against the Establishment’s knife. They stalk her. Send her death threats. She’s even been physically assaulted. But Nancy is my daughter. And I know this: She never backs down. And she never stops fighting. I want to ask you something from one parent, one patriot, to another: Will you support my daughter in the toughest battle of her life? But even in the face of all that, Nancy stood up for me. 👉 She stood up for EVERY veteran who was forgotten. 👉 She stood up for stranded American families and rescued them from an active Middle East warzone.👉 She stood up when other Republicans stayed silent. And now, she’s standing up for YOU. But she needs your backup. I may not wear the uniform anymore, but I still believe in answering the call. Will you answer it with me today? Nancy’s not running to make friends. She’s running to win. To fight. To serve. That’s what she learned growing up in our home. That’s what she learned watching me go off to war. And that’s what she’ll carry with her to the Governor’s Mansion. May God bless you and your family. With respect, General James Emory Mace (Ret.) Proud Father of Nancy Mace | | | | | | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter. Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained. At 17, she dropped out of high school and took a job slinging hash browns at Waffle House to survive. No silver spoon. No Ivy League connections. Just grit, grace, and a whole lot of graveyard shifts. By the grace of God, she turned that struggle into a story no politician can touch. She made history as the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, South Carolina’s legendary military college. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground. Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina. Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks. She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history. Team Nunn ("JFC") is a joint fundraising committee composed of Iowans for Zach Nunn ("Campaign"), Call to Service PAC ("LPAC") and NRCC (each, a "Committee," and, collectively, the "Committees"). Any contribution to the JFC permissible under the Federal Election Campaign Act, as amended ("FECA"), from contributors who have not exceeded their applicable federal contribution limits, shall be allocated among the Committees pursuant to FECA and the formula set forth in this Notice.

_**Contributions Made by an Individual or Federal Non-Multicandidate Political Committee:**_
Individuals or federal non-multicandidate PACs may contribute up to $322,100. Such contributions shall be allocated in the following order:
1\. Campaign shall receive any contribution not exceeding $7,000, designating up to $3,500 to the primary election and up to $3,500 to the general election, provided such limits apply.
2\. LPAC shall receive any contribution not exceeding $5,000 annually.
3\. NRCC shall receive for its general account any contribution not exceeding $44,300 annually.
4\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $132,900 for its Building Fund, provided such limits apply.
5\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $132,900 for its Legal Proceedings Fund, provided such limits apply.

_**Contributions Made by a Federal Multicandidate Political Committee:**_
Multicandidate PACs may contribute up to $120,000. Such contributions shall be allocated in the following order:
1\. Campaign shall receive any contribution not exceeding $10,000, designating up to $5,000 to the primary election and up to $5,000 to the general election, provided such limits apply.
2\. LPAC shall receive any contribution not exceeding $5,000 annually.
3 .NRCC shall receive for its general account any contribution not exceeding $15,000 annually.
4\. NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $45,000 for its Building Fund, provided such limits apply.
5 .NRCC shall receive any contribution not to exceed $45,000 for its Legal Proceedings Fund, provided such limits apply.

Contributions to Team Nunn, or to any participating Committee individually, are not deductible as charitable donations for federal income tax purposes. Contributions from corporations, labor organizations, national banks, federal government contractors, foreign nationals without green cards, and other federally impermissible sources are prohibited. The contributor's signature designates his or her contribution to the elections described above. Contributions that exceed a donor's contribution limit to a participating Committee shall be reallocated to the remaining Committees according to this allocation formula to the extent permitted by FECA. Any contributor may designate his or her contribution to a specific participant Committee to the extent permitted by FECA. Federal law requires us to use our best efforts to collect and report the name, mailing address, occupation, and name of employer of each individual whose aggregate contributions exceed $200 in an election cycle or calendar year, as applicable.

HAVA’s Unfinished Work By Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Junior Counsel, USGI - It has been more than twenty years since...

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/grantdemocracy/grant-report-february-5-12772040?e=c16f400a56)

---](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=00448339c2&e=c16f400a56)
| | **HAVA’s Unfinished Work
By Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Junior Counsel, USGI**It has been more than twenty years since Congress passed the Help America Vote Act (HAVA), and states are still working to get it right. Take North Carolina. For years, the state’s voter registration form marked HAVA’s mandatory identification fields (driver’s license or partial Social Security number) as optional. A citizen complaint in 2023 finally surfaced the problem, and the state eventually corrected the form—but by then, somewhere in between 100,000 and 250,000 voters had been registered without providing the required information. The issue escalated into parallel litigation: the Republican National Committee sued, and the Department of Justice followed with its own enforcement action. Each case resulted in separate consent judgments. Together, those orders require the state contact affected voters, update records, use provisional ballots for those with missing information, and report to DOJ through 2027. This was also a central issue in an election contest for a razor thin state Supreme Court race in 2024. HAVA’s voter registration identification requirement (distinct from but relevant to its separate ID rules for first-time voters) is relatively straightforward. A state cannot “accept” or “process” a registration without either the applicant’s driver’s license number or partial Social Security number (SSN), unless an applicant has neither. (And almost every voter has at least an SSN.)HAVA also establishes a clear hierarchy: an applicant with a driver’s license must provide it. Only those without one may substitute their partial SSN. The driver’s license takes priority because it’s a unique identifier that can be matched against DMV records far more reliably than a partial SSN. An investigation of states’ HAVA compliance by Grant’s sister organization Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (RITE) reveals North Carolina is not an isolated case. RITE found that multiple states’ registration forms, including [New Mexico’s and New York](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=fb9ba40169&e=c16f400a56)’s, present the two identifiers as interchangeable options, ignoring the driver’s license priority structure entirely. New York’s form instructed applicants to “make 1 selection” between the driver’s license number and partial SSN, never communicating that the driver’s license number is mandatory. To its credit, New York corrected that this week, but other states, like New Mexico, have not. New York has a second and more significant problem: a state regulation directing counties to process and approve applications missing HAVA’s required identification numbers altogether. Under this approach, applicants are registered first and asked for the missing information later, with no mechanism for rejection if they never respond. Is it any wonder that New York has the [highest proportion of registered voters nationwide](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=0da27b081b&e=c16f400a56) (23%!) lacking a driver’s license number or partial SSN?HAVA reflects a familiar legislative compromise: it imposes certain baseline requirements while leaving key implementation details to the states. That is especially true regarding the ramifications when a state is unable to match the driver’s license or Social Security number listed on the application with corresponding government databases. HAVA is reasonably clear states must make some attempt to match the information but then defers to state law on whether they can or must reject the application when it doesn’t. And state law isn’t always so clear. That gap is now the subject of RITE-supported litigation challenging a [Pennsylvania](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=730e69a05f&e=c16f400a56) directive forcing counties to accept registrations when the applicant-provided information does not match. Unlike the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA), HAVA is generally understood not to provide a private right of action, leaving enforcement largely to the Department of Justice. DOJ, however, has historically brought relatively few HAVA suits. This helps explain why compliance failures have gone undetected for years. More recently, outside groups and citizen complainants have homed in on the law and should be credited for exposing compliance problems like in North Carolina that were hiding in plain sight for over two decades. These may seem like small, technical issues, but they carry real significance. While HAVA addressed many aspects of voting, Congress placed particular emphasis on improving the accuracy of our registration lists. Lawmakers understood that registration flaws were large contributors to broader and persistent election administration problems, many of which surfaced in the 2020 Presidential Election. HAVA has undoubtedly helped address these shortcomings, but its aims won’t be fully realized until states fully comply with both the letter and spirit of the law.

| | | | |
---
| | **Arizona** Attorney General Mayes and Secretary of State Fontes are [urging county recorders to reject requests](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=95fd826685&e=c16f400a56) to hand over unredacted voter files to the DOJ, claiming it would violate state and federal laws.The [FBI subpoenaed records from the Arizona Senate](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=11758b0177&e=c16f400a56) related to the Senate’s audit of the election results from the 2020 Presidential Election for Maricopa County. Senate President Warren Petersen [shared that he complied](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=01f5735e12&e=c16f400a56) with the subpoena and supplied the requested information.**California** An advocacy group has garnered enough signatures to place a [voter ID proposition](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=2e1ca05509&e=c16f400a56) on the ballot in the upcoming election.**Colorado** A woman was sentenced to [three years in prison for fraudulently completing ballots](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=9dcd26755d&e=c16f400a56) in the name of her deceased ex-husband and her son.**Florida**[Lawmakers in Tallahassee](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=87bf122420&e=c16f400a56) passed [legislation](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=f6811815d5&e=c16f400a56) that will require documentary proof of citizenship to vote. Governor DeSantis is expected to sign this legislation into law and take effect in January 2027.After a machine and manual recount, Andy Thomson was [declared](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=0b2ff2cd04&e=c16f400a56) the new mayor of Boca Raton. Thomson led by six votes on election night, one vote after the machine recount, and ultimately won by five votes.**Indiana** Governor Braun has [signed](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=14b1be0f4f&e=c16f400a56) nine election-related bills into law, including a bill that bans ranked-choice voting.**Maine** Attorney General Frey broke with Democratic lawmakers by [telling the state Supreme Court that expanding ranked-choice](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=b8b16970bb&e=c16f400a56) voting to general elections for governor and the legislature would violate the state constitution’s requirement that those races be decided by a plurality of votes. The Republican National Committee also filed a [brief](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=009995122c&e=c16f400a56) with the court opposing the expansion.**Michigan** In a 110 page report, Attorney General Nessel [announced that her office](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=7126d873fd&e=c16f400a56) will not appeal a court ruling dismissing charges against the Republican electors from the 2020 election.37 absentee ballots in [Hamtramck’s mayoral election](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=039d28e9c2&e=c16f400a56) were left uncounted after unauthorized officials entered the city clerk’s office on election night. The officials entered the office after they saw a punching bag with a mayoral candidate’s face on it. The canvassers ultimately decided to exclude them from the results of a race decided by just 11 votes.The Michigan Department of State [wrote](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=a837951a2d&e=c16f400a56) to county clerks and election directors cautioning against using jury list questionnaire responses for list maintenance [purposes]().**Montana** Secretary of State Jacobsen [announced](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=455a344e9d&e=c16f400a56) that a new federal citizenship-verification check identified 23 voter records flagged as potential non-citizens using the Department of Homeland Security’s SAVE database. Secretary Jacobsen said the review indicated these individuals cast nearly 150 ballots in Montana elections.**Nevada** The FBI closed a voter fraud investigation where [38 noncitizens may have voted](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=1fd8eb45c3&e=c16f400a56) in the 2020 elections. Despite the findings, the FBI claims that the statute of limitations would have lapsed on any possible charges.**North Carolina** State Senate leader Phil Berger has [formally requested a recount](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=02f62b9e59&e=c16f400a56) in Guilford and Rockingham Counties, citing a 23-vote margin. On Wednesday, the State Board of Elections [denied](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=62a4583b8d&e=c16f400a56) Berger’s request for a hand-to-eye recount of 220 votes that machines flagged as under or overvotes. State law only provides for a hand-to-eye recount for a small, random sample of ballots. Wednesday’s machine recount in Guilford led to each candidate losing one vote leaving the margin unchanged.In a [parallel election protest](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=797d29aba0&e=c16f400a56), Berger alleges that at least eight Guilford County voters were issued the wrong ballot style that omitted the SD-26 race, effectively preventing them from voting in the contest and potentially warranting remedial action under state law.**Ohio** On March 17, 2026, Governor DeWine signed [legislation](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=dd59a958fb&e=c16f400a56) that largely bans ranked choice voting in the state and withholds funding from local governments that use it.**Oklahoma** A [citizen-led effort to place State Question 836 on the ballot failed](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=2ef480ce30&e=c16f400a56) after the Secretary of State determined the petition did not meet the required 172,993 valid signatures threshold, despite more than 200,000 signatures being submitted. The initiative would have placed all candidates on a single primary ballot, with party affiliated listed, and allowed every registered voter to participate in any contested race regardless of party.**Pennsylvania** Federal prosecutors [charged a Mauritanian national](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=5a4b7163d3&e=c16f400a56) with illegally voting in several federal elections including in 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, and 2024 presidential primary and general elections while unlawfully present in the United States.Matthew Laiss, a former resident of Bucks County, was [found guilty for voting twice](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=4b8d7ed1d9&e=c16f400a56) in the 2020 election. Laiss faces up to five years in prison.**Texas**[During the March 3, 2026 primary election, at least 13,000 Dallas County voters](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=73babdc5c5&e=c16f400a56) showed up at the wrong polling location, following confusion over recent rule changes.**Washington** Governor Ferguson has signed [legislation](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=fd36afe36f&e=c16f400a56) that clarifies the prohibition against double voting in the state, specifically stating that any person who intentionally votes or attempts to vote more than once in the same election or in both Washington and another state during the same election is guilty of a felony. **Wisconsin** Wisconsin election officials are [claiming that federal efforts to obtain 2020 election materials](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=10e8d1e24a&e=c16f400a56) could potentially expose how individual Milwaukee residents voted, due to state law requiring absentee ballots at central count locations to be traceable to poll book entries. Federal officials have made no attempt to subpoena or seize ballots, and Governor Evers has [said he would resist](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=eac39ab0f6&e=c16f400a56) any attempt to do so.

| | **Arizona** _**Mussi v. Fontes**_**, No. 2:24-cv-01310 (D. Ariz.)** On March 17, the Ninth Circuit [dismissed an appeal](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=1157baafd1&e=c16f400a56) from a group of Arizona Republican voters regarding alleged failures to remove ineligible voters from the state’s registration rolls. The court ruled that plaintiffs failed to adequately allege Article III standing based on vote dilution.**District of Columbia** _**Democratic Nat’l Comm. v. United States Dep’t. of Justice**_**, No. 1:26-cv-825 (D.D.C.)** On March 10, the Democratic National Committee [filed a federal lawsuit](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=4df7abc6a4&e=c16f400a56) seeking to compel the Trump administration to comply with multiple Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests regarding any plans to deploy federal agents or military personnel at polling places or election offices.**Indiana** _**Count Us In v. Diego Morales**_**, 1:25-CV-00864-RLY-MKK (S.D. Ind.)** On March 6, the state Attorney General’s Office [urged a federal court to deny a request](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=36f8711ce6&e=c16f400a56) to block the state’s ban on using student IDs for voting ahead of the 2026 election.**Iowa** _**Selcuck v. Pate**_**, No. 4:24-cv-00390 (S.D. Iowa)** On March 16, a federal court [granted](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=c11610a9c9&e=c16f400a56) the plaintiffs’ motion to dismiss all claims with prejudice and adopted the parties proposed settlement agreement in a lawsuit challenging the state’s pre-election directive flagging over 2,000 registered voters as potential noncitizens based on data from the state Department of Transportation.**Kentucky** _**United States v. Adams**_**, 3:26-cv-00019-GFVT (E.D. Ky.)** On March 10, the State Board of Elections [moved to dismiss](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=0b142298c1&e=c16f400a56) a lawsuit filed by the DOJ seeking access to the state's unredacted voter rolls.**Michigan** _**United States v. Benson**_**, No. 1:25-cv-01148 (W.D. Mich)** On March 11, the Sixth Circuit [granted in part](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=9c72696988&e=c16f400a56) the DOJ’s request for an expedited briefing schedule in its [case](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=d3048e7428&e=c16f400a56) seeking access to the state’s voter rolls. The DOJ’s principal brief is due March 23, and the state’s principal brief is due April 13.**New York** _**Serratto v. Mt. Pleasant**_**, Index No. 55442/2024 (N.Y. Sup. Ct., Westchester Cnty)** On March 10, the [Mount Pleasant Town Board voted](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=f841a7b71e&e=c16f400a56) to enter into a settlement agreement in a [suit](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=60c6151f1f&e=c16f400a56) brought by five Hispanic voters who believed their votes were diluted by the town’s current at-large voting system. Under the settlement agreement, the town will pay over a million dollars in the plaintiff’s legal fees and shift the voting system to a district-based system.**North Carolina** _**Hogarth v. Bell**_**, 5:24-cv-481 (E.D.N.C.)** On March 9, a federal court [upheld North Carolina’s ban on ballot selfies](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=8a07e1a26e&e=c16f400a56), rejecting a First Amendment challenge and finding that polling places are a nonpublic forum where reasonable, viewpoint-neutral restrictions on speech are permitted.**Pennsylvania** _**Rossman v. Schmidt**_**, No. 516 MD 2024 (Pa. Comm. Ct.)** On March 17, a county election official [urged the state Supreme Court](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=980d21ebe1&e=c16f400a56) to invalidate the state’s directive requiring counties to accept voter registration applications despite lacking identifying information required by law. This case is [sponsored by RITE](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=ae5a6e23c1&e=c16f400a56).**Virginia** _**King v. Youngkin**_**, No. 3:23-cv-00408 (E.D. Va.)** On March 9, a federal court reaffirmed an earlier ruling that a [felon’s right to vote cannot be permanently removed](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=24a409c1ec&e=c16f400a56) after the completion of the sentence.

---
|
---
| | The MacArthur Foundation [announced a $100 million commitment](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=4fe3a4c0fd&e=c16f400a56) to support democracy-focused initiatives in the United States.The Senate [voted 51-48 on Tuesday](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=ba667877d1&e=c16f400a56) to begin debate on the SAVE America Act, clearing an initial procedural hurdle for the GOP-backed bill.On March 11, the National Association of Secretaries of State [wrote](https://grantdemocracy.us21.list-manage.com/track/click?u=e037df946273cbd1eaa641b78&id=77fb1073e5&e=c16f400a56) to the White House emphasizing the need for effective and consistent communication between the federal government and state election offices as we approach the midterm elections.

His core claim is that federal statutes set a uniform day for voting not for receipt of ballots and therefore do not prohibit states from accepting ballots that arrive after Election Day if cast on time. The Supreme Court will hear oral argument in the _RNC v. Watson_ case on this issue March 23, 2026.

clean_body: HAVA’s Unfinished Work By Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Junior Counsel, USGI - It has been more than twenty years since... | | | | | | | | | HAVA’s Unfinished Work By Justin Riemer, President, USGI, and Marshal Trigg, Junior Counsel, USGIIt has been more than twenty years since Congress passed the Help America Vote Act (HAVA), and states are still working to get it right. Take North Carolina. For years, the state’s voter registration form marked HAVA’s mandatory identification fields (driver’s license or partial Social Security number) as optional. A citizen complaint in 2023 finally surfaced the problem, and the state eventually corrected the form—but by then, somewhere in between 100,000 and 250,000 voters had been registered without providing the required information. The issue escalated into parallel litigation: the Republican National Committee sued, and the Department of Justice followed with its own enforcement action. Each case resulted in separate consent judgments. Together, those orders require the state contact affected voters, update records, use provisional ballots for those with missing information, and report to DOJ through 2027. This was also a central issue in an election contest for a razor thin state Supreme Court race in 2024. HAVA’s voter registration identification requirement (distinct from but relevant to its separate ID rules for first-time voters) is relatively straightforward. A state cannot “accept” or “process” a registration without either the applicant’s driver’s license number or partial Social Security number (SSN), unless an applicant has neither. (And almost every voter has at least an SSN.)HAVA also establishes a clear hierarchy: an applicant with a driver’s license must provide it. Only those without one may substitute their partial SSN. The driver’s license takes priority because it’s a unique identifier that can be matched against DMV records far more reliably than a partial SSN. An investigation of states’ HAVA compliance by Grant’s sister organization Restoring Integrity and Trust in Elections (RITE) reveals North Carolina is not an isolated case. RITE found that multiple states’ registration forms, including ’s, present the two identifiers as interchangeable options, ignoring the driver’s license priority structure entirely. New York’s form instructed applicants to “make 1 selection” between the driver’s license number and partial SSN, never communicating that the driver’s license number is mandatory. To its credit, New York corrected that this week, but other states, like New Mexico, have not. New York has a second and more significant problem: a state regulation directing counties to process and approve applications missing HAVA’s required identification numbers altogether. Under this approach, applicants are registered first and asked for the missing information later, with no mechanism for rejection if they never respond. Is it any wonder that New York has the (23%!) lacking a driver’s license number or partial SSN?HAVA reflects a familiar legislative compromise: it imposes certain baseline requirements while leaving key implementation details to the states. That is especially true regarding the ramifications when a state is unable to match the driver’s license or Social Security number listed on the application with corresponding government databases. HAVA is reasonably clear states must make some attempt to match the information but then defers to state law on whether they can or must reject the application when it doesn’t. And state law isn’t always so clear. That gap is now the subject of RITE-supported litigation challenging a directive forcing counties to accept registrations when the applicant-provided information does not match. Unlike the National Voter Registration Act (NVRA), HAVA is generally understood not to provide a private right of action, leaving enforcement largely to the Department of Justice. DOJ, however, has historically brought relatively few HAVA suits. This helps explain why compliance failures have gone undetected for years. More recently, outside groups and citizen complainants have homed in on the law and should be credited for exposing compliance problems like in North Carolina that were hiding in plain sight for over two decades. These may seem like small, technical issues, but they carry real significance. While HAVA addressed many aspects of voting, Congress placed particular emphasis on improving the accuracy of our registration lists. Lawmakers understood that registration flaws were large contributors to broader and persistent election administration problems, many of which surfaced in the 2020 Presidential Election. I’ve been doing this job for a while now, and I’ve had the privilege to file and get on the ballot plenty of times in the Commonwealth.

**But I’ve got to tell you, this moment feels different. I truly believe this is one of – _if not the most_ – consequential elections of our lifetime.**

I don’t say that lightly, Derek.

The fact of the matter is, Trump and his administration are sowing chaos here at home, driving up everyday costs from rent to gas to groceries, and refusing to extend tax credits that lower health care costs for millions of Americans. They’re getting us into a war-of-choice in the Middle East. On top of it all, as the midterms approach, they’re attacking our free and fair elections, attempting to undermine our faith in our democracy in order to hold onto power.

I’m asking Virginians to rehire me because they deserve a senator in Washington who is willing to fight for them and stand up to this administration run amok. Working families deserve housing they can afford, health care that doesn’t break the bank, and leaders who are transparent, accountable, and actually work to improve their lives.

This November, we have the chance to hold this critical seat for Democrats and elect leaders in every corner of the Commonwealth who will put a check on Trump’s reckless agenda. We can put an end to the chaos and corruption, hold the president and his cronies to account, and turn the tide on this chapter in our history.

**But that’s only possible if this campaign has the resources and grassroots support to win this fall.**

[_**That’s why I’m asking: can you chip in today and help us reach our 10,000 Founding Donor goal? Your support couldn’t come at a more critical time.**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/127635859/608714406/1037320630?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_Different_260319_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJiMDk2YTVmMy05YjIzLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=QKrwq9z94EDVKimqbGPBDUD_7Q2-5uiAa_cOzzb1-NU=)

Regardless of whether you can give today or not, I want you to know how grateful I am to have you as a part of this team. _Thank you._

The fight continues,

Sen. Rand Paul **[confronted Sen. Markwayne Mullin](https://substack.com/redirect/048aa48f-9ba5-45dc-b321-3dccab9f61b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during his DHS secretary confirmation hearing Wednesday, accusing him of justifying the 2017 assault that left Paul with six broken ribs and a damaged lung.
## [Watch the heated moment here:](https://substack.com/redirect/048aa48f-9ba5-45dc-b321-3dccab9f61b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[](https://substack.com/redirect/048aa48f-9ba5-45dc-b321-3dccab9f61b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Click To Watch Video](https://substack.com/redirect/048aa48f-9ba5-45dc-b321-3dccab9f61b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Paul 's accusation:** Paul said he was "shocked" Mullin called him a "freaking snake" and told media he "completely understood why I had been assaulted," demanding he "tell the world why you believe I deserve to be assaulted from behind, have six ribs broken and a damaged lung!"
Paul played a compilation showing Mullin advocating bringing back canings for men to "settle" differences, saying he's "not afraid to bite" during confrontations, and previously challenging the Teamsters president to a physical fight. Paul challenged Mullin to "explain to the American public why they should trust a man with anger issues to set the proper example for ICE and Border Patrol agents" and "how a man who has no regrets about brawling in a Senate committee could set a proper example for over 250,000 men and women who work at the Department of Homeland Security."

* **What Mullin said:** Mullin didn't apologize or walk back his statements, instead saying "I don't think anybody should be hit by surprise" but "if I do have something to say, everybody in this room knows I'll come straight to you." He extended an olive branch saying "let me earn your respect, let me earn the job. I won't fail you" and "I make mistakes just like anybody else. But mistakes, if you own them, you can learn from." Paul didn't appear satisfied without an overt apology.

# **FBI investigating former counterterrorism chief Joe Kent over alleged classified information leaks**
The FBI is investigating former National Counterterrorism Center Director Joe Kent **[over allegations he leaked classified information,](https://substack.com/redirect/8395dc66-6b46-458d-903f-31b6c6ec95f9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** with the probe predating his departure from government, according to three sources. Kent resigned Tuesday citing opposition to the U.S. war against Iran, saying he "cannot in good conscience support the ongoing war," arguing Iran posed no imminent threat.
* **Why it matters:** A senior administration official told Fox News Digital that Kent was a "known leaker" who had been cut out of intelligence briefings months before his resignation. It's unclear whether the FBI investigation relates to those concerns or a separate matter. Kent, a former Army Green Beret and CIA paramilitary officer who is a Gold Star spouse, was appointed to lead the National Counterterrorism Center in early 2025.

**Tucker Carlson interviewed Kent** last night, following his departure from the administration:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b9382eac-08da-4277-aa3b-7fb7970f8be9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

# **Poll: 83% of Republicans support Trump 's Iran war despite media criticism from Tucker Carlson, Megyn Kelly**
A new J.L. Partners poll **[shared exclusively with The NY Post](https://substack.com/redirect/396065b4-76a1-48c7-b0f7-4532654ffcd1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** shows 83% of likely Republican voters "strongly" or "somewhat" support Operation Epic Fury, with just 9% opposing military action against Iran. Nearly three-quarters (74%) say the U.S. should continue until Iran's military capabilities are destroyed, while only 16% want Trump to stop immediately.
* **Why it matters:** Despite criticism from prominent podcasters Tucker Carlson and Megyn Kelly, 83% of likely Republican voters trust Trump's judgment on Iran over the former Fox News hosts (6%), with 84% agreeing with Trump's foreign policy views and 85% taking the president more seriously on world affairs than media commentators. Trump praised talk radio host Mark Levin, a staunch war supporter, calling critics "jealous and angry Human Beings" whose "sway" will "rapidly diminish."
* **The political impact:** 78% of Republican voters are more likely to support a congressional candidate who backs Trump's Iran military action in this year's midterms, while 55% would be less likely to support a GOP candidate aligned with the Carlson-Kelly camp (only 19% more likely). The poll surveyed 1,018 likely Republican voters March 17-18 with a margin of error of plus-or-minus 3.1 percentage points.

# **NYC Mayor Mamdani 's wife celebrated Palestinian plane hijacker, terrorist group in resurfaced social media posts**
NYC First Lady Rama Duwaji, 28, used **[her Tumblr account to hail Palestinian plane hijacker Leila Khaled](https://substack.com/redirect/1fc07a9f-7d67-463f-bdf2-d7b3d5b2f9fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and members of terror group Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine while living in the Middle East, according to posts reviewed by the Washington Free Beacon. In September 2017, she posted a photo of Khaled--who took part in plane hijackings in 1969 and 1970--with a caption quoting her line "if it does good for my cause, I'd be happy to accept death," then shared an image of a Bangladeshi stamp reading "we salute the valiant freedom fighters of Palestine."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1fc07a9f-7d67-463f-bdf2-d7b3d5b2f9fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

I showed up in support of the hundreds of parents and children who came to oppose **HB 5468, HB 5044, and SB 50** --and I personally testified on **HB 5554** , because that bill strikes at something even more fundamental: the system of checks and balances itself.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..fX27IFFBqWAL5SFAamuduVuqeQ5fNtRWPIW3us8BtXU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=191475840)

What I witnessed inside the Legislative Office Building mattered.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/93075c0d-7e48-4d63-9f17-f07eb9b8dc4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There were hundreds of families. It felt like an airport during a major delay--kids everywhere, long waits, overflow rooms packed. But what stood out wasn't chaos--it was the opposite.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1af6543f-fd90-4ed7-889c-0a5c9c8b3f9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_**The children were respectful, engaged, and remarkably well behaved. They played together, drew quietly, and spoke thoughtfully. I had real conversations with them. They made eye contact. They communicated clearly. They demonstrated confidence and respect.**_
# That is education.
Not just test scores or bureaucratic benchmarks--but the ability to engage, think, and interact as capable human beings. And I saw that firsthand.
These parents came from all backgrounds. Many identified as independent--unaffiliated, not ideological. But they were united on one thing:
# They want a say in how their children are raised and educated.
They showed up--despite long hours, despite discomfort, despite fear of public speaking--because staying silent was no longer an option.
Yes, there was emotion. Yes, there was anger. But when you are talking about people's children--their most precious responsibility--that emotion is not a flaw. It's a signal.
Lawmakers should not dismiss emotional testimony--they should listen more carefully to it.
**Because these were not lobbyists. Not unions. Not political machines.**
They were citizens.
**We can all agree on one thing: there are bad apples in every part of society.**
But one bad case--however serious--should not trigger a sweeping legislative overhaul that creates new problems, new bureaucracy, and new costs for thousands of families who have done nothing wrong.
Good policy is not written in reaction to the worst-case scenario.
It is built on data, proportionality, and common sense.
### _If there are gaps, fix the gaps._
### _If there are bad actors, address the bad actors._
### _But don 't treat every family like a potential case file._
# What's being proposed goes far beyond that. It moves toward building an entirely new layer of oversight--effectively a homeschooling arm within the Department of Children and Families.
That is not a measured response. That is a structural expansion of government into the daily lives of families.
And with that comes:
* Increased administrative burden
* Significant cost to taxpayers
* A presumption of risk where none has been demonstrated at scale

Policy should be precise--not punitive.
Targeted--not sweeping.
Proportionate--not reactionary.
Because when government overcorrects, it doesn't just solve a problem--it creates new ones.
Unfortunately, much of what I observed felt predetermined.
Bills like HB 5468 are advancing despite overwhelming public engagement, and there is a growing sense that outcomes are being driven along party lines rather than through genuine deliberation.
**It passed 26-20 with some flip flops despite agreement to vote against it which truly frustrated the parents after telling me about specific assurances from their elected representatives.**
# **That 's exactly why HB 5554 matters so much and why I testified.**
[](https://substack.com/redirect/28781893-c7e1-4dc9-af2c-a3702a767562?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
HB 5554 weakens one of the last meaningful bipartisan checks in Hartford. At a time when people already feel unheard, removing balance from oversight only deepens that divide.
What yesterday proved is simple:
### **The silent majority is not silent anymore.**
A supermajority is not a blank check. It is a greater responsibility--to listen, to engage, and to find common ground.
Many of the families I spoke with live by a simple principle:
### **Live and let live.**
The idea that you should be free to raise your children, educate them, and make decisions for your family--as long as you are not infringing on the rights of others.
And the reality is this:
**A homeschooled child does not interfere with anyone else 's rights.**
So the real question becomes-- **Who is actually threatened?**
Because what I saw in Hartford wasn't a problem.
It was a reminder of what's worth protecting.

clean_body: A day in the life of citizen advocates | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The Goldstein Substack - A Father-Son Publication Dr. Goldstein is Running for Congress and his page can be found A day in the life of citizen advocates | | | Mar 19| | | ∙| | Guest post ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | I showed up in support of the hundreds of parents and children who came to oppose HB 5468, HB 5044, and SB 50 --and I personally testified on HB 5554 , because that bill strikes at something even more fundamental: the system of checks and balances itself. What I witnessed inside the Legislative Office Building mattered. | | ---|---|--- There were hundreds of families. It felt like an airport during a major delay--kids everywhere, long waits, overflow rooms packed. But what stood out wasn't chaos--it was the opposite. | | ---|---|--- The children were respectful, engaged, and remarkably well behaved. They played together, drew quietly, and spoke thoughtfully. I had real conversations with them. They made eye contact. They communicated clearly. They demonstrated confidence and respect. That is education. Not just test scores or bureaucratic benchmarks--but the ability to engage, think, and interact as capable human beings. And I saw that firsthand. These parents came from all backgrounds. Many identified as independent--unaffiliated, not ideological. But they were united on one thing: They want a say in how their children are raised and educated. They showed up--despite long hours, despite discomfort, despite fear of public speaking--because staying silent was no longer an option. Yes, there was emotion. Yes, there was anger. But when you are talking about people's children--their most precious responsibility--that emotion is not a flaw. It's a signal. Lawmakers should not dismiss emotional testimony--they should listen more carefully to it. Because these were not lobbyists. Not unions. Not political machines. They were citizens. We can all agree on one thing: there are bad apples in every part of society. But one bad case--however serious--should not trigger a sweeping legislative overhaul that creates new problems, new bureaucracy, and new costs for thousands of families who have done nothing wrong. Good policy is not written in reaction to the worst-case scenario. It is built on data, proportionality, and common sense. If there are gaps, fix the gaps. If there are bad actors, address the bad actors. But don 't treat every family like a potential case file. What's being proposed goes far beyond that. It moves toward building an entirely new layer of oversight--effectively a homeschooling arm within the Department of Children and Families. That is not a measured response. That is a structural expansion of government into the daily lives of families. And with that comes: Increased administrative burden Significant cost to taxpayers A presumption of risk where none has been demonstrated at scale Policy should be precise--not punitive. Targeted--not sweeping. Proportionate--not reactionary. Because when government overcorrects, it doesn't just solve a problem--it creates new ones. Unfortunately, much of what I observed felt predetermined. Bills like HB 5468 are advancing despite overwhelming public engagement, and there is a growing sense that outcomes are being driven along party lines rather than through genuine deliberation. It passed 26-20 with some flip flops despite agreement to vote against it which truly frustrated the parents after telling me about specific assurances from their elected representatives. That 's exactly why HB 5554 matters so much and why I testified. HB 5554 weakens one of the last meaningful bipartisan checks in Hartford. At a time when people already feel unheard, removing balance from oversight only deepens that divide. What yesterday proved is simple: The silent majority is not silent anymore. A supermajority is not a blank check. It is a greater responsibility--to listen, to engage, and to find common ground. Many of the families I spoke with live by a simple principle: Live and let live. The idea that you should be free to raise your children, educate them, and make decisions for your family--as long as you are not infringing on the rights of others. And the reality is this: A homeschooled child does not interfere with anyone else 's rights. So the real question becomes-- Who is actually threatened? Because what I saw in Hartford wasn't a problem. It was a reminder of what's worth protecting. | | ---|---|--- | A guest post by| Consultant, Political Consultant, Campaign Manager, Construction Consultant and Corporate Attorney.
