body:
This isn’t about politics. It’s about whether the powerful play by the same rules as the rest of us.

| | | | | [|
---](https://ericburlisonforcongress.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b6500a115da3c4344522b1e48&id=c0738fe625&e=5f9dc01b8c)
| | Peter ,

On Tuesday, I told you about the Clinton deposition. Today I want to tell you why it matters and why the people who don’t want these questions asked are hoping this story dies quietly.Here’s how Washington works. Powerful people surround themselves with lawyers, PR teams, and political allies whose only job is to run out the clock. They stall. They deflect. They say “I don’t recall” until the cameras move on and the public forgets.They’re counting on that happening right now.Think about what we know. Jeffrey Epstein had extraordinary access to the most powerful people in the world. He visited the Clinton White House 17 times. His associate Ghislaine Maxwell was so close to the family she attended Chelsea’s wedding and skipped a federal deposition to do it. These aren’t conspiracy theories. These are facts entered into the record.And when I asked Hillary Clinton about them under oath? Her attorneys intervened to block questions. She deflected responsibility to her husband and her daughter. On almost everything substantive, she claimed she couldn’t remember.This isn’t about party. The subpoena was bipartisan. This is about whether there’s one set of rules for the powerful and another for everyone else.I believe the American people already know the answer. And that’s why I’m not going to stop.More to come on Friday.For Missouri,

name: Joe Jaworski
subject: He survived Afghanistan. He died in Texas.
disclaimer_text: paid for by Joe Jaworski Campaign
body:
He made it out of Afghanistan alive. And then, here in Texas, he was taken into ICE custody and died within 24 hours. | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/jaworskifortexas.com/last-night-14193519?e=5d8d80652b)
---
| | [ ](https://jaworskifortexas.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2e1f50319ad85f5f9e5c11ac9&id=5dd1cd674d&e=5d8d80652b)
---
| | , He survived Afghanistan. [**And then he came to Texas, where he died. You can read the story by clicking this link.**](https://jaworskifortexas.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2e1f50319ad85f5f9e5c11ac9&id=91d494bcbf&e=5d8d80652b) Mr. Paktyawal was an Afghan interpreter who worked alongside American Special Forces for years in a war zone where you could die every day. He risked everything to help our troops. When the Taliban took over, interpreters like him were hunted and killed. **He did what we asked of him. He stood with us. And in 2021, he and his family were evacuated to safety in the United States, just as they should have been.** He made it out alive. Then he came to Texas, where Trump's masked forces seized him while he was taking his kids to school, and dumped him in a caged pen where he lasted 24 hours. **Everything about that is wrong. Does America have any honor left? Do we?** This man was not a stranger to our country. He was part of our mission. He was someone who stood with American forces when it mattered most. People like Mr. Paktyawal are the reason many Americans came home alive. And this is how his story ends? **Let me be clear.** **If justice is more than just a word, then someone in Texas government should immediately open an investigation into Mr. Paktyawal’s death.** This is not abstract to me. In my day job, I mediate Defense Base Act cases. These are claims brought by American and foreign military contractors injured while serving in places like Afghanistan, Iraq, and Syria. I have handled thousands of these cases, including many for Afghan nationals and Afghan Americans who put their lives on the line as interpreters for our military. I know who these men and women are. I know what they gave. I know what they risked. Mr. Paktyawal survived a war zone. He should not have died like this in Texas. **The Texas Attorney General should investigate this death. Immediately. Thoroughly. Transparently.** **Justice demands it.** And as someone asking for your vote to serve as your next Attorney General, I am telling you exactly where I stand. I will never look the other way when something like this happens. Not to a citizen. Not to an immigrant. Not to someone who served alongside Americans in war. We are better than this. Or at least we are supposed to be. [**If you believe in a more just country and a more just Texas, I'm asking you to help me deliver that. Give what you can, but know that I will always stand and fight those who wish to do our people harm. Citizen or immigrant, I will fight for you.**](https://jaworskifortexas.us17.list-manage.com/track/click?u=2e1f50319ad85f5f9e5c11ac9&id=7109ac8185&e=5d8d80652b) Onward,

**

clean_body: He made it out of Afghanistan alive. And then, here in Texas, he was taken into ICE custody and died within 24 hours. | | | | | | | , He survived Afghanistan. Mr. Paktyawal was an Afghan interpreter who worked alongside American Special Forces for years in a war zone where you could die every day. He risked everything to help our troops. When the Taliban took over, interpreters like him were hunted and killed. He did what we asked of him. He stood with us. And in 2021, he and his family were evacuated to safety in the United States, just as they should have been. He made it out alive. Then he came to Texas, where Trump's masked forces seized him while he was taking his kids to school, and dumped him in a caged pen where he lasted 24 hours. Everything about that is wrong. Does America have any honor left? Do we? This man was not a stranger to our country. He was part of our mission. He was someone who stood with American forces when it mattered most. People like Mr. Paktyawal are the reason many Americans came home alive. And this is how his story ends? Let me be clear. If justice is more than just a word, then someone in Texas government should immediately open an investigation into Mr. Paktyawal’s death. This is not abstract to me. In my day job, I mediate Defense Base Act cases. These are claims brought by American and foreign military contractors injured while serving in places like Afghanistan, Iraq, and Syria. I have handled thousands of these cases, including many for Afghan nationals and Afghan Americans who put their lives on the line as interpreters for our military. I know who these men and women are. I know what they gave. I know what they risked. Mr. Paktyawal survived a war zone. He should not have died like this in Texas. The Texas Attorney General should investigate this death. Immediately. Thoroughly. Transparently. Justice demands it. And as someone asking for your vote to serve as your next Attorney General, I am telling you exactly where I stand. I will never look the other way when something like this happens. Not to a citizen. Not to an immigrant. Not to someone who served alongside Americans in war. We are better than this. Or at least we are supposed to be. name: Niki Conforti
subject: A Huge Win!
body:
A Huge Win! | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/33f8a3cc54cc/conforti-for-congress-10613398?e=25f4fa3311)
---
| | |
---
| | | Dear Peter,

What a big win! I'd like to express a heartfelt thank you to all those that made it to the polls to vote for me. I am humbled by the outpouring of support and trust in my leadership to represent you in Congress.

A huge thank you to the many that got involved to make this victory possible. Whether you placed a sign in your yard or walked in a day of action or spoke highly of me to a friend or neighbor, it made a difference. And thank you to my team of volunteers and my family for their hard work, love and support. I could not have done this without them.

Now, we look to November and to a win in the General Election. The people of the 6th district have been frustrated for too long by the lack of proper representation. If I have the honor of representing this district in Congress, I will work to represent the whole district and address issues that will benefit us all. I will take action to lower the cost of living and improve the lives of the people in this district, and all Americans. I will work to protect families and children from the threats we face here at home. Peace will be a focus, keeping our young men and women home, not fighting in foreign wars. First and foremost, I will work to preserve American values and our way of life.

The race to November starts now. The people of the 6th Congressional District deserve better. And I will do my best to provide a voice for you in Congress.

It will take all of us working together to win in November. Get involved.

Standing Together We Will Win!

[](https://conforti4congress.us6.list-manage.com/track/click?u=7fd34b7284bf7f5e87a4e45e5&id=18dee5f5ee&e=25f4fa3311)

Your support is greatly appreciated.
---
| Thank you,

Niki Conforti
Candidate
Illinois 6th Congressional District

Hello --
This is Steve Kerr, reaching out about an issue that is near and dear to my heart: _Ending gun violence in America._
I lost my father to gun violence when I was 18 years old. I know the pain people feel when they get that call. I don’t wish that on anyone.
I am sick and tired of our politicians offering their “thoughts and prayers” but doing nothing to actually stop gun violence. There’s so much more we can and need to do to stop this epidemic in our country.
**[Gabby Giffords has helped lead the fight to save lives from gun violence, but she can’t do it alone. Will you make your first contribution of the year to my friends at GIFFORDS before their midnight deadline?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260319-1-b&t=4&akid=11324%2E3935704%2ECyK_zD)
**[DONATE](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260319-1-b&t=5&akid=11324%2E3935704%2ECyK_zD)**
Give me a minute to explain why your donation to GIFFORDS is so important, especially today.
The amount of lives lost from gun violence is heartbreaking. Every time you see another mass shooting on the news, it should be a reminder that there are tools to help stop this.
80% of people want universal background checks. That alone could save hundreds, if not thousands, of lives every year. But right now, the gun lobby is spending millions to fearmonger and stop that progress from happening.
We have a decision to make: _Are we going to continue to let the gun lobby run us over? Will we continue letting our children go to school terrified every day? Or do we want to actually take action to protect each other?_
That’s what democracy is about. We must demand that our representatives listen to us and fight to save lives. If they don’t, then we need to replace them with leaders who actually give a damn.
**So team, I am asking:** **[Will you rush in a donation to GIFFORDS PAC today? Your donations will help GIFFORDS get the resources to stand up against the gun lobby ahead of the midterm elections.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260319-1-b&t=6&akid=11324%2E3935704%2ECyK_zD)

Peter,

fiercely anti-Israel candidate and would-be Squad member. POLITICO: AIPAC
attacks fall flat as Democrat Daniel Biss wins Illinois House primary

The Israel lobby group won just half of the congressional seats they spent
$21 million trying to buy, and $12 million of that was in losing races —
but they’re bragging about defeating Kat Abughazaleh because their chosen
candidate came in THIRD place.

They claim these victories prove that “being pro-Israel is good policy and
good politics,” but the reality is their brand and platform are so toxic
that they had to hide behind shadow PACs to secretly fund their chosen
candidates and avoid even mentioning Israel in any of the ads they ran.

a $21 million bet on Illinois — outspending everyone in every primary —
and lost 2 races & barely won another despite outspending their opponents
more than 5:1.

The moral of the story is their money isn't enough to buy every race, and

body:
Through my experience, I've learned that the fights that matter most often happen at the state level, especially in state supreme courts.
# [](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/18?refcode=em20260319-1248&t=1&akid=1256%2E294397%2EtF-wAA)
I’ve spent much of my career fighting to protect the foundations of our democracy — from defending voting rights as the 82nd Attorney General of the United States to working to protect the voice of the people in elections across the country.
Through my experience, I've learned that the fights that matter most often happen at the state level, _especially_ in state supreme courts.
I've also seen what happens when those courts get captured by extremists backed by dark money. We see judges who put a political agenda ahead of the law, and ahead of the people.
**That brings me to what’s happening in Wisconsin.**
This state has been at the center of some of the biggest fights over democracy and voting rights in our country. On April 7, there's a Wisconsin Supreme Court election that we all need to turn our attention to.
Right-wing special interests have hand-picked their candidate, Maria Lazar — someone with a clear record of embracing extreme positions and even conspiracy theories — and they're ready to spend whatever it takes to put her on the bench.
These are the same forces that spent years trying to pack the courts with judges who will do their bidding and undermine our democracy.
**I’ve seen this playbook before, and I know how it ends if we don't fight back.**
**_That’s why I’m throwing my support behind Judge Chris Taylor._** She’s the real deal. As an attorney, a public servant, and a judge, she's spent her career protecting the rights and freedoms of every Wisconsinite.
But she needs our help to compete against the dark money flooding into Wisconsin as you read this.
That’s why I’m asking: [**Will you chip in $10 today to help Judge Chris Taylor win a seat on the Wisconsin Supreme Court?**](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/31?c0=em_ms_jct_20260319_1_ak.Nuihlj&amount=10&refcode=em20260319-1248&t=3&akid=1256%2E294397%2EtF-wAA)

If we want courts that protect our freedoms and uphold the rule of law, we have to fight for them.
Thank you for taking action,
Eric H. Holder, Jr.
82nd United States Attorney General

FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASEMarch 19, 2026katherine@julialetlow.com
**State Senator Stewart Cathey Jr. Endorses Julia Letlow for U.S. Senate** _Cathey becomes the latest Republican leader to back Letlow’s campaign for the U.S. Senate._
**Baton Rouge, LA** \- Today, Congresswoman Julia Letlow, the Trump-endorsed candidate for U.S. Senate in Louisiana, announced she has received the endorsement of State Senator Stewart Cathey Jr., Chairman of the Louisiana Senate Agriculture Committee. This marks another major show of support from Republican leaders across Louisiana.
Senator Cathey, who represents Louisiana’s 33rd Senate District and leads one of the most important committees for the state’s farmers and rural communities, praised Rep. Letlow’s conservative leadership and record of delivering for North Louisiana families.
_“Julia Letlow has proven she is a true conservative who puts Louisiana first,”_**said Senator Cathey.** _“As Chairman of the Agriculture Committee, I know how important it is to have leaders who understand the needs of our farmers, our rural communities, and our small businesses. Julia has delivered for our state, fought for infrastructure and disaster recovery, and stood firm on the values that matter most. Louisiana needs someone in the U.S. Senate who knows how to get results and won’t back down from a fight – and that’s Julia.”_
Rep. Letlow expressed her appreciation for Cathey’s support and his leadership in the State Senate.
_“I’m grateful for Senator Cathey’s endorsement,”_**said Rep. Letlow** _. “We share a commitment to protecting our conservative values, strengthening our rural communities, and ensuring Louisiana has a powerful voice in Washington. I’m grateful for his partnership and his support.”_
Rep. Letlow currently represents Louisiana’s 5th Congressional District and serves on the House Education and the Workforce Committee and the House Appropriations Committee, where she has worked to secure funding for flood mitigation, infrastructure improvements, and economic development projects benefiting communities across the state.
With Senator Cathey’s endorsement, the Letlow campaign continues to build strong grassroots and elected official support statewide.
For more information, visit [JuliaLetlow.com](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=738ac74101&e=95355a072c).

Friends —
On March 26, the U.S. marks Equal Pay Day —the point when women’s earnings finally catch up to what men made in all of 2025.
In other words, women had to work nearly three extra months to earn what men made in one year.
And at the current pace, full pay equity won’t arrive until 2071 —even later for many women of color.
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/AV/AVEMR/1/81321/images/Numbers%20behind%20gap.png]
Closing the pay gap isn’t just an economic issue—it’s a policy issue. The decisions made in statehouses and Congress shape workplace protections, pay transparency, childcare access, and economic opportunity.
That’s why Emerge trains Democratic women to run for office and win. Across the country right now, hundreds of women are preparing to lead—from school boards to Congress.
But building this pipeline of women leaders requires early investment.
If you believe the fight for equal pay can’t wait another generation, will you support Emerge today?

subject: What the end of the Voting Rights Act would mean

body:
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
@ariberman.bsky.social: SCOTUS decision killing what’s left of Voting Rights Act could cost Dems 19 House seats, eliminate every majority-minority district in South, eviscerate 14th/15th Amendments & fulfill John Roberts 40-year crusade against country’s most important civil rights law [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=031926_1&amount=25]
The impact shows how partisan this all is, Team. A complete dismantling of the Voting Rights Act -- a key civil rights law -- would only harm one political party and return parts of the country to a suppressive era we left behind sixty years ago.
During the oral arguments in Louisiana v. Callais , at least five conservative justices seemed ready to handicap the VRA so that it will no longer stop white majorities from locking racial minorities out of elected office through racial gerrymandering.
The consequences are simple to understand and grave for voter participation. The harder we make it to vote, the more politicians make voter participation feel worthless, the less people actually take part. Needless to say, the less people who participate, the less our democracy and our government looks like the people it's supposed to represent.
Team: We have to spread the word about this case and the consequences of dismantling the Voting Rights Act. Step up with $35 or whatever you can today and help us defend the right to vote >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=031926_1&amount=35]

At issue in the case is Section 2 of the VRA, which requires that racial minorities have an equal opportunity to meaningfully participate in the electoral process. This provision has been used to strike down districting schemes and maps that prevented Black voters and other racial minorities from electing their preferred representatives. Since 1965, Section 2 has given people of color a seat at the table, from school boards to the halls of Congress. It appears this 60-year era is coming to an end.
We've said it before and will say it again, but it's been clear long before the MAGA movement that Chief Justice Roberts has seen the removal of the VRA as one of his top goals for his time on the Court. It appears he may be on the cusp of succeeding.
Striking down the last remnants of the Voting Rights Act is exactly why the Supreme Court held this case over from last year. Gutting Section 2 would take us backwards in time and allow racial gerrymandering to be a standard practice, silencing more voters. Just like the redistricting fights across the country, this is all about whether the party in power can choose their voters in order to stay in power in perpetuity.
We simply can't afford to go backwards like this. Will you chip in with $35 or more to help us fight back against these partisan efforts to silence voters? >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=031926_1&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
https://www.facebook.com/voteraction [https://www.facebook.com/voteraction] https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org [https://bsky.app/profile/voteractionproject.org] https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/ [https://www.instagram.com/voteractionproj/] https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/ [https://www.linkedin.com/company/voter-action-project/]
Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.
Your support is crucial to our efforts. Will you donate today to help us protect voting rights? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=031926_1&amount=20]

subject: I Won’t Stay Silent About This
body:
This war is illegal and unjustified

| | | | | [|
---](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=bf1b68c1b6&e=53c7d12fc7)
| | | | | | [](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=db8e3c92f7&e=53c7d12fc7)
Dear Peter,
The United States is sliding into a war with Iran — and Congress didn’t even vote on it.
**That’s not just wrong. It’s unconstitutional.**
A senior intelligence official just resigned, making it clear: Iran posed no imminent threat. This isn’t defense. This is a political decision — one that could cost lives.
**Our system was designed to stop exactly this.** The power to declare war belongs to Congress so no president can drag us into conflict on a whim.
But that only works if the people in Congress actually do their job.
**Brad Sherman won’t.**
For thirty years, he’s built a career on keeping his head down, avoiding risk, and staying just quiet enough to never be held accountable. Right now, when it actually matters, he’s doing exactly what he’s always done.
**Nothing.**
Let’s be clear about what that means: more blank checks for war, more lives on the line, and more working families here at home footing the bill while they’re already struggling to get by.
**Silence isn’t strategy. It’s surrender.**
I’m running for Congress because I refuse to be quiet while this happens. I will fight to stop unauthorized wars, push for diplomacy, and actually use this office to check a president who thinks he can act without consequence.
If you’re done with politicians who hide when it matters most, then this campaign is yours too.
[**Chip in right now and help us replace silence with something a hell of a lot louder.**](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=fb09bc31b5&e=53c7d12fc7)

| Earlier this month, 1,000,908 Texans voted for me as Texas Attorney General.
Peter, that's more than a million people who showed up to say they want something better for Texas -- an AG's Office that works for us, not Washington DC; an AG who respects the rule of law and enforces it; a system of government where checks and balances are leveraged effectively and as often as needed to hold power accountable.
I'm deeply grateful for every single one of those votes.
But as you know, this race isn't over yet.
Despite earning nearly twice as many votes as our opponent, our race for Attorney General is headed to a runoff. That means the next few weeks will determine everything.
Peter, runoff elections can be odd and unpredictable. The campaigns that stay the most organized, increase momentum, and have the resources to mobilize and inspire our base are the ones that win runoffs. We're doing that work right now, Peter.
We're already halfway through the month, and the truth is that runoffs are won right now -- in the weeks when campaigns are organizing, inspiring voters to turn out again, and building the resources to finish the job. Our emails are the best way to make sure you stay updated on Nathan's campaign for AG, but if you'd no longer like to hear from Team Johnson, please click the "unsubscribe" link below. | | == | Earlier this month, 1,000,908 Texans voted for me as Texas Attorney General. Peter, that's more than a million people who showed up to say they want something better for Texas -- an AG's Office that works for us, not Washington DC; an AG who respects the rule of law and enforces it; a system of government where checks and balances are leveraged effectively and as often as needed to hold power accountable. I'm deeply grateful for every single one of those votes. But as you know, this race isn't over yet. body:

In America, we’re in the fight of our lifetime and the fight for the lives of the next generation. The ending of Roe signaled the end of abortion in America, but the abortion industry pivoted, and tragically we see more abortions now than before Roe was ended.

But the days of the abortion pill may be numbered, thanks to courageous leaders like my friend U.S. Senator Josh Hawley, who is calling on Congress to ban the abortion pill mifepristone. I joined him at his press conference last week, where I was able to share my heart for the unborn and for the women victimized by the abortion industry.

Also, this week, you will hear the raw, unfiltered stories about the abortion pill. From a woman who nearly died and can never have children again, to a former Planned Parenthood director turned whistleblower who won in court, to young moms sharing gut-wrenching testimonies of coercion, trauma, and even abortion pill reversal. _**WATCH BREAKTHROUGH HOUR: EPISODE 6**_

### The World Baseball Classic felt like a reflection of something bigger
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/@theangrydem)
---
| Mar 19
---
| [](https://substack.com/@theangrydem)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3159258&post_id=191485064&utm_source=substack&isFreemail=true&submitLike=true&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkxNDg1MDY0LCJyZWFjdGlvbiI6IuKdpCIsImlhdCI6MTc3MzkzNTIyOCwiZXhwIjoxNzc2NTI3MjI4LCJpc3MiOiJwdWItMzE1OTI1OCIsInN1YiI6InJlYWN0aW9uIn0.5LPeurDVuiGy6YuTmONKbiGVarfdasjWZR-qatgcmiU&utm_medium=email&utm_campaign=email-reaction&r=1hvr60)

---
| | [](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3159258&post_id=191485064&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkxNDg1MDY0LCJpYXQiOjE3NzM5MzUyMjgsImV4cCI6MTc3NjUyNzIyOCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTMxNTkyNTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.vBm-rk1rhoUY3N26Ym64WnvjOtog4oN3J-Euqr-VJi8)
---
| | [](https://substack..mLwZvgZ9KqPR9sNz9I8byYIsTlUanr4osdcLZTfcrZc?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/mattdiemer/p/the-version-of-america-the-world?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

For the past couple weeks the **World Baseball Classic** has captured most of my attention.
What struck me was not just the baseball. It was what it revealed. It felt like an allegory of the United States. Not the version we tell ourselves, but the version the rest of the world might actually see.
It brought me back to something I have not thought about in years. **The 2010 World Expo in Shanghai.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8fc0ffb7-8877-46f4-9e55-0740ac63cf01?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
2010 USA Expo pavilion
I remember being there. Walking through pavilion after pavilion, seeing how countries chose to present themselves. It was not just architecture. It was identity. It was culture. It was pride.
China's pavilion felt rooted in history. Chile's felt warm and inviting, almost like a gathering place. Other countries leaned into innovation, agriculture, art, and storytelling. There was a sense of energy and authenticity. You could feel that these countries wanted to show the world who they were.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3fcbf826-71ef-447d-a832-a0afd8809114?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
2010 China Expo Pavilion
And then there was the United States.
Our pavilion was funded by corporate sponsorships. That was the law. It could not be publicly funded. So what we ended up with was something that felt exactly like what funded it.
Corporate.
Structured.
Controlled.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/6b8239fd-c627-4008-9e57-2a3e525a5ca3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The USA Expo Wall of Culture
There were logos everywhere. Sponsorships from major corporations. A overly polished presentation. A Disney-produced film as the centerpiece. Everything felt managed, filtered, and corporate.
It also felt empty.
People walked through it and wanted more. Not more production value. More substance. More culture. More identity. Real America.
Even working there felt different. Other countries had camaraderie. Their teams bonded. They explored together. There was joy. There was pride in representing something.
Ours felt like a corporate environment. Rules. Image control. PR management. A sense that you were representing a brand more than your slice of Americana.
I remember leaving early. Not because I did not want to be there, but because I was disappointed. I knew we had more to offer than the American Airlines branded uniforms.
That same feeling came back watching the World Baseball Classic.
You look at teams like Venezuela, the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico, Italy, even teams like the Czech Republic. You see energy. You see joy. You see players dancing in the dugout, celebrating, embracing the moment. You see teams that are proud to be there.
You see connection.
Then you look at Team USA.
And it feels different.
Team Venezuela on the left the man credited with killing Osama bin Laden giving a speech to Team USA on the right
There is talent. There is no question about that. But the energy is not the same. The urgency is not the same. The joy is not the same.
You hear about contract concerns. Commitments to MLB teams. Players not fully bought in until they arrive. A sense that this is not the main event.
You see a locker room that feels controlled instead of alive.
You see moments that lean into something else entirely. Military symbolism. Structured messaging. A kind of seriousness that does not match the spirit of the competition.
There was even a moment where the team brought in the man credited with killing Osama bin Laden to give a pregame speech. That choice, paired with the heavy military symbolism throughout, pushed the tone away from sport and into something that felt more paramilitary than celebratory.
It did not feel like a team coming together around the joy of representing their country. It felt like a performance of power.
And you start to notice something else.
It feels like we expect to win. It felt like the performances were mailed in.
There was a moment where the United States played as if advancement was guaranteed, without even realizing they had not clinched a semifinal spot, ultimately leaving it up to other teams.
It is not confidence. It is arrogance and complacency.
And when you put that next to teams that are fighting for every inning, celebrating every moment, and treating the opportunity like it matters, the contrast becomes obvious.
It reminded me of that feeling in Shanghai.
When you put the United States next to the rest of the world, something becomes clearer.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/50ea7820-e77a-4588-b008-623aaa821564?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
USA Shanghai expo menu sponsored by KFC
We are not lacking talent. We are not lacking resources. We are not lacking history or culture.
What we are lacking, at least in how we present ourselves, is connection.
We are starting to feel like a brand instead of a country.
Because I do not believe that is who we actually are.
I do not believe that Americans lack heart, or pride, or community. I know it exists.
But I do think something else is shaping how we show up.
Corporate influence.
Militarization.
You see it in our cities. You drive through different towns and they start to look the same. The same stores. The same layouts. The same developments. The same experience.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/79b43107-fe6f-4c8d-b2bd-a8190111a079?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The new Main Street USA
And compared to countries that are willing to show their culture in a raw, vibrant, and sometimes imperfect way, we start to look... flat.
That is the word that keeps coming to mind.
Flat.
The World Baseball Classic showed that.
Not because we lost a game. Baseball is unpredictable. Anyone can win on any given day. That is part of what makes it great.
The Cleveland Guardians proved that. A young, scrappy team that fought their way back and played with energy and belief.
That is what I saw in those international teams.
And it made me ask a harder question.
What are we showing the world right now?
Because when people show you who they are, you are supposed to believe them. And I think, on that stage, we showed something.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a80c3469-9129-4cc2-95ad-33f8fdc5bd7b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Not the full picture. Not the best version of ourselves. But a version that is shaped by corporate influence, controlled messaging, and a belief that we will always come out on top no matter what.
It is not wrong to be confident, but it is wrong to be arrogant.
It is about asking: **Are showing the world who we really are?**
Because I know we are more than what I saw in Shanghai.
And I know we are more than what I saw in that dugout.
We have to keep fighting for the identity within our communities and not being afraid to export it.
## Stay Angry.

**" Federal judge extends school voucher application window for Texas families"** via [Fort Worth Star-Telegram](https://substack.com/redirect/82ac0a54-9644-4f40-835f-4f858d33c52c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - Texas parents have an additional two weeks to apply for the state's new school voucher program after a federal judge in Houston extended the application deadline on Tuesday just hours before the window was set to close.

The extension comes after no Islamic schools in Texas were approved for the program while thousands of other schools have been. U.S. District Judge **Alfred Bennett** called that fact "troubling" before issuing a temporary restraining order to extend the window.

The new deadline to apply for the state voucher program is March 31.

Several Islamic schools in Texas are suing Comptroller **Kelly Hancock** , claiming the state blocked Islamic schools from the $1 billion private school voucher program because of their religion.

**Eric Hudson** , an attorney for those suing the state, said Tuesday that the goal of his clients was to ensure the application window did not block parents. (_[FWST](https://substack.com/redirect/8c8b5106-738b-41e5-9ec9-56e4a75a9878?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" RodeoHouston increasing security after fights cause chaos in carnival area"** via [KHOU](https://substack.com/redirect/bf7267e5-4e0c-4d05-bc56-398a384f6c4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - RodeoHouston is increasing security after fights caused chaos in the carnival area and forced an early closure Saturday. Officials say security responded quickly and are taking steps to prevent similar incidents from happening again.

The Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo says it is taking steps to prevent fights that led to chaos and the early closure of the carnival Saturday night.

Videos circulating on social media show large groups fighting in the middle of a crowded carnival area, prompting some guests to run and creating confusion among families attending the event.

Witnesses said they were unsure what sparked the violence, but officials said security and law enforcement responded quickly.

One of the witnesses who recorded video of the fight, **Damion Potts** , described the moment the chaos began.
"I seen the dude throw the punch, and then after that it was just -- I didn't know who was with who. I just seen punches thrown, kicks," Potts said.

Potts said the situation changed quickly once authorities arrived.

"I feel like the police were on alert, and once the horses got there, I think a lot of people scattered," Potts said.

(_[KHOU](https://substack.com/redirect/ad557d9d-772f-49ef-8f1a-e4381470f8d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" A plan to get more electricity to West Texas may come undone"** [San Antonio Report's](https://substack.com/redirect/7c490a1e-b190-49f8-a1c0-fa525ed5d131?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Carlos Nogueras Ramos, The Texas Tribune** - A plan to get more electricity to West Texas may come undone ODESSA -- If Texas wants to continue to be a leader in oil, the Permian Basin needs more energy.

That's the warning influential trade groups representing oil companies have been telling state lawmakers and regulators for years.

A dearth of power plants and transmission lines connecting the region to the rest of the state's grid means there isn't enough electricity to power field operations, such as compressors and oil pumps.

In 2023, lawmakers offered a solution that spelled out a dramatic expansion of electricity transmission infrastructure in the Permian Basin, the state's biggest oil field.

"Texas' thriving production is driving the state's success," the Texas Oil and Gas Association, a statewide trade group whose membership makes up roughly 90% of the state's crude oil and natural gas market, wrote to regulators charged with designing that plan. "And a reliable electricity supply is crucial to sustaining this industry."

(_[SA REPORT](https://substack.com/redirect/16bee406-0ce8-4e0c-9b98-06ecbd2d564d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Why an East Texas rancher donated part of his water rights to the state"** [The Texas Tribune's](https://substack.com/redirect/44ad1f30-6c59-4c96-ade1-7b91e6cf51cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Alejandra Martinez** - **Bob Sanders** bumps along the dirt roads of his 1,100-acre ranch in a beat up burgundy Chevrolet Suburban, the engine roaring as his sprawling cattle operation, known locally for its wagyu beef, stretches around him. A shotgun rides in the passenger seat and battered binoculars sit on the dashboard.

The sloping pasture where his rust-colored cows graze gives way to trees that flank a narrow ribbon of water. It doesn't look like much, just a slow-moving channel threading through sweetgums and cypress, but this 2.6-mile stretch of the Big Cypress Bayou carries a lot of weight -- it connects Lake O' the Pines, the region's main water supply, to Caddo Lake, the state's only natural lake.

Water feels abundant in the area. But even in this lush corner of the state, water is increasingly top of mind. For Sanders and many of his neighbors, the bayou represents something increasingly fragile in Texas: water that still belongs to the landscape it came from.

That was partly the reason why Sanders took a step few Texans have taken in decades. He donated part of his water rights to the Texas Water Trust, a little-known program that allows people to give their water rights to the state for environmental protection.

(_[TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/63fcea67-06c4-4ca3-ba43-a383796b5f86?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Texas A&M's new Fort Worth campus opens this fall. Here's what to know"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/e3f1d271-3aae-4b27-8da3-fcc953098f70?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - Students will soon be able to study at **Texas A &M University**'s new Fort Worth campus. The downtown campus, which broke ground in 2023, is opening its first building and starting classes this fall.

The campus will house degree-granting programs from Texas A&M University and **Tarleton State University** , which is part of the A&M System. Texas A&M-Corpus Christi's Center for Advanced Aviation Technologies will have a research presence, and six state agencies will be on campus as well.

Officials say the campus will help fill the region's growing talent and research needs by collaborating in key area industries including health care, aerospace, and media and entertainment. Fort Worth, Tarrant County and Texas A&M leaders are also working to build a mixed-use innovation district around the campus that will connect companies with the university, startups and other businesses to foster economic development.

(_[DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/e5dcdd01-fb9d-454e-a6b3-2c2920c59e5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)
* * *
* **2026**

**" With no Trump endorsement, Cornyn, Paxton let deadline to remove names from ballot pass"** [Houston Chronicle's](https://substack.com/redirect/2f600f67-fc62-4419-be86-ca5925f9329c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **James Osborne** - Neither U.S. Sen. **John Cornyn** nor Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** filed Tuesday to end their candidacy in the GOP runoff for Texas' U.S. Senate seat on May 26, meaning both will appear on the ballot regardless of a promised endorsement from President Donald Trump.

Tuesday at 5 p.m. was their last chance to remove their names from the ballot under Texas election law. With still no endorsement in the race from Trump, both candidates signaled Tuesday they were digging in for what is expected to be a savage and costly campaign.

ornyn's campaign launched ads highlighting reports of Paxton's infidelity, with the musical refrain, "Ken's love shack." The Texas senator told a reporter from Semafor, "if the president decides to endorse, I certainly would welcome that, but we're not waiting around."

Meanwhile, Paxton directed attention to a voter ID bill in Congress that Trump has endorsed but Senate Majority Leader John Thune -- a Cornyn ally -- has said has little chance of passing. Cornyn reversed course last week when he said he supports ending the rule allowing the minority party to filibuster legislation they oppose, but many GOP senators still support the more than century-old practice aimed at creating bipartisan law.

(_[HOU CHRON](https://substack.com/redirect/2f600f67-fc62-4419-be86-ca5925f9329c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Texas primaries spotlight growing perils of polling as forecasts miss the mark"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/7961cce0-69f7-40df-b548-2a7779916ed4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - Pollsters at the University of Texas at Tyler predicted about a week before the primary that U.S. Rep. **Jasmine Crockett** would cruise to the Democratic nomination for Senate with 55% of the vote. She lost.

A survey by Emerson College the weekend before the March 3 primary gave Attorney Gen. **Ken Paxton** a solid lead over Sen. **John Cornyn** in the GOP Senate showdown. Voters instead left him in second place, sending both to a runoff.

And a poll released on the eve of the primary by YouGov, an online research firm, predicted Cornyn would get barely a third of the Republican vote. He beat that by 10 points.

Such are the perils of polling in which thin samples, shaky turnout guesses and voters who increasingly refuse to answer surveys can produce numbers that look precise but badly misread the electorate.

When those numbers are amplified by campaigns, media and political operatives, they can shape expectations about races that the actual vote quickly shatters.

(_[DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/2d974fd6-bdd4-4ac4-be5b-2ed2eeb8728f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Dallas GOP will OK countywide voting sites for May 26 runoff"** [The Texas Tribune's](https://substack.com/redirect/b3eaba5e-fff1-4d99-856b-72745b6678a2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Natalia Contreras** - Dallas County Republicans will agree to allow voters to cast ballots at countywide voting sites for the May 26 runoff election after a switch to precinct-based voting sites caused chaos, the county party chair said Tuesday.

**Allen West** , Dallas County Republican Chair, supported the use of precinct-based sites earlier this month, but said using precincts again for the runoff would expose the county party to "increased risk and voter confusion" because the county is planning to use countywide sites for upcoming municipal elections and early voting.

(_[TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/8a903efb-4af8-41f6-aa1b-4f05fff677e9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Binkley drops bid for Texas' 32nd Congressional District"** [The Texas Tribune's](https://substack.com/redirect/3cd220d9-a52b-4251-b591-566c42ce656e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Gabby Birenbaum** - Richardson businessman and pastor **Ryan Binkley** on Tuesday withdrew from the GOP primary runoff for a North Texas congressional district redrawn for Republicans, leaving conservative attorney **Jace Yarbrough** as the GOP nominee and presumptive next congressman.

**Ryan Binkley** , who ran a quixotic presidential campaign in 2024, finished second in the March 3 Republican primary for Texas' 32nd Congressional District. He received 22% of the vote to Yarbrough's 49%, narrowly forcing a runoff.

But hours before the deadline for candidates to withdraw from the May 26 runoff ballot, Binkley announced he would drop out of the race and back Yarbrough.

"Now it is time to come together," Binkley said. "Our party is strongest when we stand united, and I am committed to doing my part to help us secure a strong showing in November."
(_[TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/93d0b53f-fc2e-4a1b-b44e-f77a22b5bc35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Early voting starts Tuesday for Houston City Council District C race"** [ABC13 Houston's](https://substack.com/redirect/4b5b0794-afba-4368-9707-06ba32c2c345?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **None** - Early voting starts Tuesday for Houston City Council District C race When District C Councilmember **Abbie Kamin** resigned to run for Harris County Attorney, she left open a seat that represents much of Houston's core, including Montrose, the Heights, and Meyerland, 35-square miles with a population of 215,000.

She also sent voters back to the polls early to choose a new council member for her unfinished term.

**Nancy Sims** is a political science lecturer at the University of Houston.

"I would call this one of the most grassroots campaigns I've seen in years," Sims told ABC13. "The candidates in the race are just real neighborhood-oriented people. They span the cross-section of the district in that they are from different communities."

There are seven candidates, including four women and three men. All of whom are campaigning for votes, with different experiences and different priorities.

"So, this is for the person who gets your street fixed, your potholes filled, your trash picked up, you know, a day-to-day working city council member," Sims said.
Whoever wins will fill the unfinished term, which runs until January.

(_[ABC13 Houston](https://substack.com/redirect/9246eaea-d45e-4639-a90a-77d152405bf2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)
* * *
* **STATE GOVERNMENT**

**" DFPS requests court intervention in foster care management in North Texas, 3 years after awarding contract to private group"** via [WFAA](https://substack.com/redirect/df8ff21f-a1cd-4245-9926-54ad4e470449?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - DFPS requests court intervention in foster care management in North Texas, 3 years after awarding contract to private group WFAA has reported on several issues involving EMPOWER's leadership in the region. **The Texas Department of Family and Protective Services (DFPS)** filed a request for a court to consider tapping a third-party entity to take over foster care case management in nine North Texas counties on Monday.

It's been just more than three years since DFPS awarded a contract to EMPOWER to oversee case management for foster children in Dallas, Collin, Ellis, Rockwall, Grayson, Fannin, Navarro, Hunt and Kaufman counties. These counties make up Region 3E, or Metroplex East, in the department's geographic map.

Once DFPS investigates and determines it is necessary to remove a child from their home, it has been EMPOWER's responsibility to assign each child a caseworker, find safe placements for each child and maintain oversight of their safety since fully taking over case management in March 2024. It's part of what DFPS calls community-based care (CBC), a statewide model to contract private groups to manage foster care throughout Texas on a regional level.

(_[WFAA](https://substack.com/redirect/cb055f2e-3add-47b9-bbc3-fa0aea50a544?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)
* * *
* **LOCAL GOVERNMENT**

**" Corpus Christi water emergency may be just two months away, city leaders say"** [The Texas Tribune's](https://substack.com/redirect/f92d0622-75ed-4c20-8c32-2c18bdc81faf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Alejandra Martinez** - Corpus Christi leaders on Tuesday unveiled new projections suggesting that the city could be just two months away from triggering emergency water measures.

At a marathon city council meeting that stretched for 10 hours, **Nick Winkelmann** , interim chief operating officer of Corpus Christi Water, outlined five potential scenarios -- two of which would push the city into a level one water emergency by May. At that point, the city's water supply would be projected to fall short of demand within 180 days.

When pressed by council member **Kaylynn Paxson** on which scenario the city is preparing to follow, staffers at the water utility said they expect to narrow the possibilities down to two or three in the coming weeks as more data becomes available.

**" Dallas mayor calls City Hall debate 'silly games,' defends review of options"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/64e080f3-2760-4de2-984d-e8271eaaca01?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - Dallas Mayor**Eric Johnson** pushed back Sunday against friction over City Hall's future as "silly games" meant to "muddy the waters," saying exploring relocation options is routine due diligence, not a backroom scheme.

In his weekly newsletter, Johnson outlined his most detailed case yet for studying whether Dallas should move City Hall, saying speculation and sensational coverage have distorted the debate.

"Those who are more interested in muddying the waters than dealing in facts are working overtime, trying to make normal stuff sound nefarious," Johnson said.

The mayor said the core issue is simple: the I.M. Pei-designed City Hall is aging, expensive to maintain and ill-suited for modern government operations.

"Dallas City Hall isn't in good shape," Johnson said. "It doesn't meet the needs of a modern big-city government -- or, really, of any modern workplace."

He said the building's design anchors a government district that leaves a large stretch of downtown underused and does not serve the city's current needs.

TEA keeps details at a minimum"** via [Fort Worth Star-Telegram](https://substack.com/redirect/1b220612-bdc1-4a04-a1b0-1a52be8c9a15?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - Texas Education Commissioner **Mike Morath** recently announced he's planning to share his Fort Worth ISD appointments for the board of managers and a new superintendent "in the coming weeks." The replacement of district leaders comes after a 10-month saga involving appeals from the district attempting to stop state intervention, which was triggered by a campus receiving five failed accountability ratings in a row from the state.

Amid a pending state takeover of the Fort Worth Independent School District, the Texas Education Agency has declined to release similar background information for superintendent candidates that it had already released for board of managers candidates.

Although some information about board of managers applicants has been released, details on superintendent candidates have mostly remained under wraps. In early March, Morath announced current Superintendent **Karen Molinar** , who applied to keep her job amid the takeover, will be replaced.

His stepfather, firefighter **Bobbie Cook** , said the city of Fort Worth made it hard for Halvorson to get treatment for his injuries.

In July 2024, Fort Worth police officer **Bobbie Sanchez** was working a vehicle burglary detail when she was elbowed in the face by a suspect she was apprehending. The force of the blow dislocated Sanchez's jaw, permanently damaging both her temporomandibular joints, which connect the jawbone to the skull.

For nearly two years, Sanchez has lived with pain in her head, jaw, neck and shoulders, and it's likely she'll never be the same.

That much Sanchez has accepted. What she can't accept are the hoops she said she and other police officers and firefighters have had to jump through to get medical care under the city of Fort Worth's workers' compensation program.

"What I want people to hear most is that my horrible experience is not unique," Sanchez wrote in a message to the Star-Telegram.

**" Federal judge extends school voucher application window for Texas families"** via [Fort Worth Star-Telegram](https://substack.com/redirect/ad899d01-a61c-4233-9b57-48dd8df225c7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - Texas parents have an additional two weeks to apply for the state's new school voucher program after a federal judge in Houston extended the application deadline on Tuesday just hours before the window was set to close.

The extension comes after no Islamic schools in Texas were approved for the program while thousands of other schools have been. U.S. District Judge **Alfred Bennett** called that fact "troubling" before issuing a temporary restraining order to extend the window.

The new deadline to apply for the state voucher program is March 31.

Several Islamic schools in Texas are suing Comptroller **Kelly Hancock** , claiming the state blocked Islamic schools from the $1 billion private school voucher program because of their religion.

**Eric Hudson** , an attorney for those suing the state, said Tuesday that the goal of his clients was to ensure the application window did not block parents. **" A plan to get more electricity to West Texas may come undone"** [San Antonio Report's](https://substack.com/redirect/ff234d72-0a85-4bfc-b9b1-f030de7c58eb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Carlos Nogueras Ramos, The Texas Tribune** - A plan to get more electricity to West Texas may come undone ODESSA -- If Texas wants to continue to be a leader in oil, the Permian Basin needs more energy.

That's the warning influential trade groups representing oil companies have been telling state lawmakers and regulators for years.

A dearth of power plants and transmission lines connecting the region to the rest of the state's grid means there isn't enough electricity to power field operations, such as compressors and oil pumps.

In 2023, lawmakers offered a solution that spelled out a dramatic expansion of electricity transmission infrastructure in the Permian Basin, the state's biggest oil field.

"Texas' thriving production is driving the state's success," the Texas Oil and Gas Association, a statewide trade group whose membership makes up roughly 90% of the state's crude oil and natural gas market, wrote to regulators charged with designing that plan. "And a reliable electricity supply is crucial to sustaining this industry."

(_[SA REPORT](https://substack.com/redirect/8c302c99-d892-4e42-bf94-b50af1f2e965?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Why an East Texas rancher donated part of his water rights to the state"** [The Texas Tribune's](https://substack.com/redirect/2dd224e6-d839-4f0c-8014-65e770dc5ab3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Alejandra Martinez** - **Bob Sanders** bumps along the dirt roads of his 1,100-acre ranch in a beat up burgundy Chevrolet Suburban, the engine roaring as his sprawling cattle operation, known locally for its wagyu beef, stretches around him. A shotgun rides in the passenger seat and battered binoculars sit on the dashboard.

The sloping pasture where his rust-colored cows graze gives way to trees that flank a narrow ribbon of water. It doesn't look like much, just a slow-moving channel threading through sweetgums and cypress, but this 2.6-mile stretch of the Big Cypress Bayou carries a lot of weight -- it connects Lake O' the Pines, the region's main water supply, to Caddo Lake, the state's only natural lake.

Water feels abundant in the area. But even in this lush corner of the state, water is increasingly top of mind. For Sanders and many of his neighbors, the bayou represents something increasingly fragile in Texas: water that still belongs to the landscape it came from.

That was partly the reason why Sanders took a step few Texans have taken in decades. He donated part of his water rights to the Texas Water Trust, a little-known program that allows people to give their water rights to the state for environmental protection.

(_[TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/b1a41d32-0151-48c6-81e0-b0e53417e281?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

Here's what to know"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/d4d98e96-aa96-4fc1-9cfa-8c36c1a69a5c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - Students will soon be able to study at **Texas A &M University**'s new Fort Worth campus. The downtown campus, which broke ground in 2023, is opening its first building and starting classes this fall.

The campus will house degree-granting programs from Texas A&M University and **Tarleton State University** , which is part of the A&M System. Texas A&M-Corpus Christi's Center for Advanced Aviation Technologies will have a research presence, and six state agencies will be on campus as well.

Officials say the campus will help fill the region's growing talent and research needs by collaborating in key area industries including health care, aerospace, and media and entertainment. Fort Worth, Tarrant County and Texas A&M leaders are also working to build a mixed-use innovation district around the campus that will connect companies with the university, startups and other businesses to foster economic development.

**" With no Trump endorsement, Cornyn, Paxton let deadline to remove names from ballot pass"** [Houston Chronicle's](https://substack.com/redirect/cf719919-f44e-4002-b340-0757c39a2dbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **James Osborne** - Neither U.S. Sen. **John Cornyn** nor Texas Attorney General **Ken Paxton** filed Tuesday to end their candidacy in the GOP runoff for Texas' U.S. Senate seat on May 26, meaning both will appear on the ballot regardless of a promised endorsement from President Donald Trump.

Tuesday at 5 p.m. was their last chance to remove their names from the ballot under Texas election law. With still no endorsement in the race from Trump, both candidates signaled Tuesday they were digging in for what is expected to be a savage and costly campaign.

ornyn's campaign launched ads highlighting reports of Paxton's infidelity, with the musical refrain, "Ken's love shack." The Texas senator told a reporter from Semafor, "if the president decides to endorse, I certainly would welcome that, but we're not waiting around."

Meanwhile, Paxton directed attention to a voter ID bill in Congress that Trump has endorsed but Senate Majority Leader John Thune -- a Cornyn ally -- has said has little chance of passing. Cornyn reversed course last week when he said he supports ending the rule allowing the minority party to filibuster legislation they oppose, but many GOP senators still support the more than century-old practice aimed at creating bipartisan law.

(_[HOU CHRON](https://substack.com/redirect/cf719919-f44e-4002-b340-0757c39a2dbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Texas primaries spotlight growing perils of polling as forecasts miss the mark"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/9051edfb-7169-4ce0-9212-0d49e23bcdea?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - Pollsters at the University of Texas at Tyler predicted about a week before the primary that U.S. Rep. **Jasmine Crockett** would cruise to the Democratic nomination for Senate with 55% of the vote. She lost.

A survey by Emerson College the weekend before the March 3 primary gave Attorney Gen. **Ken Paxton** a solid lead over Sen. **John Cornyn** in the GOP Senate showdown. Voters instead left him in second place, sending both to a runoff.

And a poll released on the eve of the primary by YouGov, an online research firm, predicted Cornyn would get barely a third of the Republican vote. He beat that by 10 points.

Such are the perils of polling in which thin samples, shaky turnout guesses and voters who increasingly refuse to answer surveys can produce numbers that look precise but badly misread the electorate.

When those numbers are amplified by campaigns, media and political operatives, they can shape expectations about races that the actual vote quickly shatters.

(_[DMN](https://substack.com/redirect/351a1ac2-ec35-4eb8-ae52-2d62cd16e74f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**Allen West** , Dallas County Republican Chair, supported the use of precinct-based sites earlier this month, but said using precincts again for the runoff would expose the county party to "increased risk and voter confusion" because the county is planning to use countywide sites for upcoming municipal elections and early voting.

**" Binkley drops bid for Texas' 32nd Congressional District"** [The Texas Tribune's](https://substack.com/redirect/c51127f6-6636-4fed-beca-bf6f61a730ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Gabby Birenbaum** - Richardson businessman and pastor **Ryan Binkley** on Tuesday withdrew from the GOP primary runoff for a North Texas congressional district redrawn for Republicans, leaving conservative attorney **Jace Yarbrough** as the GOP nominee and presumptive next congressman.

**Ryan Binkley** , who ran a quixotic presidential campaign in 2024, finished second in the March 3 Republican primary for Texas' 32nd Congressional District. He received 22% of the vote to Yarbrough's 49%, narrowly forcing a runoff.

But hours before the deadline for candidates to withdraw from the May 26 runoff ballot, Binkley announced he would drop out of the race and back Yarbrough.

"Now it is time to come together," Binkley said. "Our party is strongest when we stand united, and I am committed to doing my part to help us secure a strong showing in November."
(_[TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/2c978e72-9c4d-476b-bf94-3577e7ac620a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Early voting starts Tuesday for Houston City Council District C race"** [ABC13 Houston's](https://substack.com/redirect/43c9eece-6921-4c3c-a520-9362843e907d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **None** - Early voting starts Tuesday for Houston City Council District C race When District C Councilmember **Abbie Kamin** resigned to run for Harris County Attorney, she left open a seat that represents much of Houston's core, including Montrose, the Heights, and Meyerland, 35-square miles with a population of 215,000.

She also sent voters back to the polls early to choose a new council member for her unfinished term.

**Nancy Sims** is a political science lecturer at the University of Houston.

"I would call this one of the most grassroots campaigns I've seen in years," Sims told ABC13. "The candidates in the race are just real neighborhood-oriented people. They span the cross-section of the district in that they are from different communities."

There are seven candidates, including four women and three men. All of whom are campaigning for votes, with different experiences and different priorities.

"So, this is for the person who gets your street fixed, your potholes filled, your trash picked up, you know, a day-to-day working city council member," Sims said.
Whoever wins will fill the unfinished term, which runs until January.

**" DFPS requests court intervention in foster care management in North Texas, 3 years after awarding contract to private group"** via [WFAA](https://substack.com/redirect/27ae884e-11c5-4566-a889-976a461cf9c1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - DFPS requests court intervention in foster care management in North Texas, 3 years after awarding contract to private group WFAA has reported on several issues involving EMPOWER's leadership in the region. **The Texas Department of Family and Protective Services (DFPS)** filed a request for a court to consider tapping a third-party entity to take over foster care case management in nine North Texas counties on Monday.

It's been just more than three years since DFPS awarded a contract to EMPOWER to oversee case management for foster children in Dallas, Collin, Ellis, Rockwall, Grayson, Fannin, Navarro, Hunt and Kaufman counties. These counties make up Region 3E, or Metroplex East, in the department's geographic map.

Once DFPS investigates and determines it is necessary to remove a child from their home, it has been EMPOWER's responsibility to assign each child a caseworker, find safe placements for each child and maintain oversight of their safety since fully taking over case management in March 2024. It's part of what DFPS calls community-based care (CBC), a statewide model to contract private groups to manage foster care throughout Texas on a regional level.

(_[WFAA](https://substack.com/redirect/44bf5643-c1a9-4312-a8da-e1c0c4a0066c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Corpus Christi water emergency may be just two months away, city leaders say"** [The Texas Tribune's](https://substack.com/redirect/25c60a35-ae67-4349-b527-02e256dc7de6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) **Alejandra Martinez** - Corpus Christi leaders on Tuesday unveiled new projections suggesting that the city could be just two months away from triggering emergency water measures.

At a marathon city council meeting that stretched for 10 hours, **Nick Winkelmann** , interim chief operating officer of Corpus Christi Water, outlined five potential scenarios -- two of which would push the city into a level one water emergency by May. At that point, the city's water supply would be projected to fall short of demand within 180 days.

When pressed by council member **Kaylynn Paxson** on which scenario the city is preparing to follow, staffers at the water utility said they expect to narrow the possibilities down to two or three in the coming weeks as more data becomes available.

Meanwhile, **Greg Abbott** -- who sharply criticized Corpus Christi leaders for their handling of the crisis recently -- has ordered agencies to suspend normal procedures in an effort to buy the city more time.
(_[TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/bf9384c0-888d-40d3-9223-f600e0231fd2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_)

**" Dallas mayor calls City Hall debate 'silly games,' defends review of options"** via [Dallas Morning News](https://substack.com/redirect/7d259b5d-2216-4a76-a083-dca69b116e4a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - Dallas Mayor**Eric Johnson** pushed back Sunday against friction over City Hall's future as "silly games" meant to "muddy the waters," saying exploring relocation options is routine due diligence, not a backroom scheme.

In his weekly newsletter, Johnson outlined his most detailed case yet for studying whether Dallas should move City Hall, saying speculation and sensational coverage have distorted the debate.

"Those who are more interested in muddying the waters than dealing in facts are working overtime, trying to make normal stuff sound nefarious," Johnson said.

The mayor said the core issue is simple: the I.M. Pei-designed City Hall is aging, expensive to maintain and ill-suited for modern government operations.

"Dallas City Hall isn't in good shape," Johnson said. "It doesn't meet the needs of a modern big-city government -- or, really, of any modern workplace."

He said the building's design anchors a government district that leaves a large stretch of downtown underused and does not serve the city's current needs.

The replacement of district leaders comes after a 10-month saga involving appeals from the district attempting to stop state intervention, which was triggered by a campus receiving five failed accountability ratings in a row from the state.

Amid a pending state takeover of the Fort Worth Independent School District, the Texas Education Agency has declined to release similar background information for superintendent candidates that it had already released for board of managers candidates.

His stepfather, firefighter **Bobbie Cook** , said the city of Fort Worth made it hard for Halvorson to get treatment for his injuries.

In July 2024, Fort Worth police officer **Bobbie Sanchez** was working a vehicle burglary detail when she was elbowed in the face by a suspect she was apprehending. The force of the blow dislocated Sanchez's jaw, permanently damaging both her temporomandibular joints, which connect the jawbone to the skull.

For nearly two years, Sanchez has lived with pain in her head, jaw, neck and shoulders, and it's likely she'll never be the same.

That much Sanchez has accepted. What she can't accept are the hoops she said she and other police officers and firefighters have had to jump through to get medical care under the city of Fort Worth's workers' compensation program.

"What I want people to hear most is that my horrible experience is not unique," Sanchez wrote in a message to the Star-Telegram.

The Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo says it is taking steps to prevent fights that led to chaos and the early closure of the carnival Saturday night. () " A plan to get more electricity to West Texas may come undone" Carlos Nogueras Ramos, The Texas Tribune - A plan to get more electricity to West Texas may come undone ODESSA -- If Texas wants to continue to be a leader in oil, the Permian Basin needs more energy. That's the warning influential trade groups representing oil companies have been telling state lawmakers and regulators for years. A dearth of power plants and transmission lines connecting the region to the rest of the state's grid means there isn't enough electricity to power field operations, such as compressors and oil pumps. In 2023, lawmakers offered a solution that spelled out a dramatic expansion of electricity transmission infrastructure in the Permian Basin, the state's biggest oil field. "Texas' thriving production is driving the state's success," the Texas Oil and Gas Association, a statewide trade group whose membership makes up roughly 90% of the state's crude oil and natural gas market, wrote to regulators charged with designing that plan. "And a reliable electricity supply is crucial to sustaining this industry." () " Why an East Texas rancher donated part of his water rights to the state" Alejandra Martinez - Bob Sanders bumps along the dirt roads of his 1,100-acre ranch in a beat up burgundy Chevrolet Suburban, the engine roaring as his sprawling cattle operation, known locally for its wagyu beef, stretches around him. A shotgun rides in the passenger seat and battered binoculars sit on the dashboard. The sloping pasture where his rust-colored cows graze gives way to trees that flank a narrow ribbon of water. It doesn't look like much, just a slow-moving channel threading through sweetgums and cypress, but this 2.6-mile stretch of the Big Cypress Bayou carries a lot of weight -- it connects Lake O' the Pines, the region's main water supply, to Caddo Lake, the state's only natural lake. Water feels abundant in the area. But even in this lush corner of the state, water is increasingly top of mind. For Sanders and many of his neighbors, the bayou represents something increasingly fragile in Texas: water that still belongs to the landscape it came from. That was partly the reason why Sanders took a step few Texans have taken in decades. He donated part of his water rights to the Texas Water Trust, a little-known program that allows people to give their water rights to the state for environmental protection. That’s the warning influential trade groups representing oil companies have been telling state lawmakers and regulators for years.

A dearth of power plants and transmission lines connecting the region to the rest of the state’s grid means there isn’t enough electricity to power field operations, such as compressors and oil pumps.

In 2023, lawmakers offered a solution that spelled out a dramatic expansion of electricity transmission infrastructure in the Permian Basin, the state’s biggest oil field.

“Texas’ thriving production is driving the state’s success,” the Texas Oil and Gas Association, a statewide trade group whose membership makes up roughly 90% of the state’s crude oil and natural gas market, wrote to regulators charged with designing that plan. “And a reliable electricity supply is crucial to sustaining this industry.”

**“Why an East Texas rancher donated part of his water rights to the state”** [The Texas Tribune’s](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/MVEW6t9IhR4y2ULSxfQmgByUGqzsOMBmBmJwttxW%2BkfdBNfIegrrFfaIJCOn%0AoxvZ64Tk54BQrxBaIWlrfmcNlugmfrcyI866GToJ1tthOa%2B6C1bVkNNQ7WNj%0ABN5Mp2zFpP%2Bm92yXjrYHVvK6KbQDKW9QaHQyJNOXZctTl7wZbx0%3D%0A/46b26e1bf881c1ed) **Alejandra Martinez** – **Bob Sanders** bumps along the dirt roads of his 1,100-acre ranch in a beat up burgundy Chevrolet Suburban, the engine roaring as his sprawling cattle operation, known locally for its wagyu beef, stretches around him. A shotgun rides in the passenger seat and battered binoculars sit on the dashboard.

The sloping pasture where his rust-colored cows graze gives way to trees that flank a narrow ribbon of water. It doesn’t look like much, just a slow-moving channel threading through sweetgums and cypress, but this 2.6-mile stretch of the Big Cypress Bayou carries a lot of weight — it connects Lake O’ the Pines, the region’s main water supply, to Caddo Lake, the state’s only natural lake.

Water feels abundant in the area. But even in this lush corner of the state, water is increasingly top of mind. For Sanders and many of his neighbors, the bayou represents something increasingly fragile in Texas: water that still belongs to the landscape it came from.

That was partly the reason why Sanders took a step few Texans have taken in decades. He donated part of his water rights to the Texas Water Trust, a little-known program that allows people to give their water rights to the state for environmental protection.

**“Texas primaries spotlight growing perils of polling as forecasts miss the mark”** via [Dallas Morning News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/nPAj1uWd9kdhRxDg3TwtyzyZ7xatFeyVuQeQaaxHt1avUeWAoz7R7iL2uZmX%0AzrI9T%2F0MijpyNyseFoSuOM5vEjO%2B02tjChr0BSvOwMTJJu5sdmQDSH7iYQKx%0ArPmowqc6Ie1ZeilV9Sn5i87y9Ma3KEyQsLiBaXV3a825b%2BCPtQM%3D%0A/7fb1355433102053) – Pollsters at the University of Texas at Tyler predicted about a week before the primary that U.S. Rep. **Jasmine Crockett** would cruise to the Democratic nomination for Senate with 55% of the vote. She lost.

A survey by Emerson College the weekend before the March 3 primary gave Attorney Gen. **Ken Paxton** a solid lead over Sen. **John Cornyn** in the GOP Senate showdown. Voters instead left him in second place, sending both to a runoff.

And a poll released on the eve of the primary by YouGov, an online research firm, predicted Cornyn would get barely a third of the Republican vote. He beat that by 10 points.

Such are the perils of polling in which thin samples, shaky turnout guesses and voters who increasingly refuse to answer surveys can produce numbers that look precise but badly misread the electorate.

When those numbers are amplified by campaigns, media and political operatives, they can shape expectations about races that the actual vote quickly shatters.

**Ryan Binkley** , who ran a quixotic presidential campaign in 2024, finished second in the March 3 Republican primary for Texas’ 32nd Congressional District. He received 22% of the vote to Yarbrough’s 49%, narrowly forcing a runoff.

But hours before the deadline for candidates to withdraw from the May 26 runoff ballot, Binkley announced he would drop out of the race and back Yarbrough.

She also sent voters back to the polls early to choose a new council member for her unfinished term.

**Nancy Sims** is a political science lecturer at the University of Houston.

“I would call this one of the most grassroots campaigns I’ve seen in years,” Sims told ABC13. “The candidates in the race are just real neighborhood-oriented people. They span the cross-section of the district in that they are from different communities.”

There are seven candidates, including four women and three men. All of whom are campaigning for votes, with different experiences and different priorities.

“So, this is for the person who gets your street fixed, your potholes filled, your trash picked up, you know, a day-to-day working city council member,” Sims said.
Whoever wins will fill the unfinished term, which runs until January.
