body:
Chris Rabb is the clear progressive choice in the nation’s bluest district.
#
Breaking news, Peter:
**Justice Democrats is endorsing a 13th Democratic primary candidate this cycle: State Representative Chris Rabb in Pennsylvania’s 3rd congressional district!**
[](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260319-2-cr.pz-meD&refcode=em20260319-37584&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=37584%2E1203867%2EZjNC4J)
**[This is our next primary fight, and it’s coming up two months from today on May 19th. Rush a grassroots donation to directly support Chris’s campaign now!](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260319-2-cr.pz-meD&refcode=em20260319-37584&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=37584%2E1203867%2EZjNC4J)**
Our movement suffered some tough losses this week against a monumental amount of spending from AIPAC, Crypto, and AI. While we’re disappointed, we’re not going to let it slow us down one bit.
**We are turning our anger into more fights against the establishment and corporate Super PACs, and uniting the progressive movement to get right back in the ring to support Rep. Rabb in Philadelphia.**
Chris is a trailblazing, anti-establishment progressive who has spent the last 8 years representing a majority-Black, mixed-income district of nearly 70,000 people across 4 neighborhoods in Philadelphia.
He’s established a record of taking on corporate power and Republican extremism to serve the needs of everyday people — and Philadelphians deserve that leadership in Washington.
**PA-03 is the nation’s bluest congressional district, and this open primary race is the first one it’s experienced in the last 35 years.** That makes it a prime opportunity to build our bloc and elect a bold, progressive champion for working people.
Chris is running to put community over commerce, expand democracy, abolish ICE, strengthen workers’ rights, guarantee access to healthcare through Medicare for All, housing, clean air and water, end US-backed forever wars & genocide, and confront the danger that concentrated wealth poses to real self-government.
He is committed to dismantling systems of oppression, ending pay-to-play politics, and building a government that answers to voters, _not billionaires and corporate lobbyists._
That’s why our movement is coming together to make clear that Chris is the progressive choice for Philadelphia. Justice Democrats is proud to join fellow progressive groups Working Families Party, One PA, and Philadelphia Democratic Socialists of America, along with Philadelphia City Council Minority Leader Kendra Brooks and Minority Whip Nicolas O’Rourke, in endorsing Chris for Congress.
**[Chris is the CLEAR progressive choice for this open seat, so let’s give him a surge of support in these last nine weeks before election day. Pitch in $5 or more today — 100% of it will go directly to his campaign.](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260319-2-cr.pz-meD&refcode=em20260319-37584&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=4&akid=37584%2E1203867%2EZjNC4J)**
**[Contribute $5](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260319-2-cr.pz-meD&refcode=em20260319-37584&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=23&akid=37584%2E1203867%2EZjNC4J)**
In solidarity,
Alexandra Rojas
Executive Director

name: Chaz Molder
subject: “I’ve never voted for a Democrat before, but…”
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Molder for Congress
body:
I shared this story when I sat down with Bob Mueller.

| | | | |
---
Peter, I recently had the chance to sit down with Bob Mueller to discuss this campaign and my vision for Middle Tennessee. Being on Bob’s show reminded me of something from when I was growing up here in Columbia. When I was a kid, my grandmother and I used to watch Bob’s show together in her living room. Back then, politics felt different. People disagreed, but there wasn’t the same sense of anger or tension around public service. That difference hit me when I told my daughter I was running for Congress. The first thing that came out of her mouth was “Daddy, does that mean someone might hurt you?” That stopped me in my tracks. Politics shouldn’t feel that way to our kids, and it’s one reason I believe we need to turn the temperature down. That’s how I’ve tried to lead as mayor of Columbia. In a town like ours, you learn quickly that potholes don’t have partisan labels. People just want leaders who will solve problems. I see that across TN-5. A few weeks back at a baseball game, a man came up to me and said, “I’ve never voted for a Democrat before, but I’m voting for you.” Moments like that tell me people are ready for leadership focused on real issues — rising costs, uncertainty for farmers and small businesses, and building stronger communities. clean_body: I shared this story when I sat down with Bob Mueller. | | | | | Peter, I recently had the chance to sit down with Bob Mueller to discuss this campaign and my vision for Middle Tennessee. Being on Bob’s show reminded me of something from when I was growing up here in Columbia. When I was a kid, my grandmother and I used to watch Bob’s show together in her living room. Back then, politics felt different. People disagreed, but there wasn’t the same sense of anger or tension around public service. That difference hit me when I told my daughter I was running for Congress. The first thing that came out of her mouth was “Daddy, does that mean someone might hurt you?” That stopped me in my tracks. Politics shouldn’t feel that way to our kids, and it’s one reason I believe we need to turn the temperature down. That’s how I’ve tried to lead as mayor of Columbia. In a town like ours, you learn quickly that potholes don’t have partisan labels. People just want leaders who will solve problems. I see that across TN-5. A few weeks back at a baseball game, a man came up to me and said, “I’ve never voted for a Democrat before, but I’m voting for you.” Moments like that tell me people are ready for leadership focused on real issues — rising costs, uncertainty for farmers and small businesses, and building stronger communities. If you’d like to hear more from my conversation with Bob Mueller, you can check it out here: ~~ ~~ | | ~~ Thanks for coming along for the ride. — Chaz | | ---|---|--- About Chaz Molder Chaz Molder is the Mayor of Columbia, Tennessee, serving since 2019 and re-elected in 2022. A Columbia native and graduate of the University of Tennessee and the University of Memphis Law School, he returned home to build a career in law and public service. subject: Donald Trump never got the memo
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY SHAPIRO FOR PENNSYLVANIA
body:
We’ve built something special here in Pennsylvania

Here’s the thing about public service: It’s called service for a reason. You’re there to serve others, not yourself. But that memo never made it to Donald Trump or all the Congressional Republicans who’ve profited huge sums of money from their elected office — all while raising costs, gutting health care, and screwing over the good people of Pennsylvania. **Pennsylvanians deserve a government that works for them, Derek. Not for a President. Not for a handful of special interests._Them._** A government that protects our fundamental rights, not one that dismantles them. A government that expands freedom and opportunity for all. Not one that saves those opportunities for a select, wealthy few. body:
President Trump took to Truth Social to endorse my opponent and attack me – just minutes after a brand-new poll came out showing this race statistically tied.

It's Roy Cooper here. This changes everything. Early Monday morning, President Trump took to Truth Social to endorse my opponent and attack me – just minutes after a brand-new poll came out showing this race statistically tied. Lately, I've been doing some reflecting on my grandfather, President John F. Kennedy, and his legacy of hope.
In my run to fight for NY-12 in Congress, and just as a person, that's what I want to focus on. Hope.
My name is Jack, or John Bouvier Kennedy Schlossberg if you want to know the whole thing.
In high school, I spent hours watching my grandfather's speeches. He taught us all that politics isn't about serving yourself — it's about serving others. When we fight for hope, we're not just doing it for ourselves, we're doing it for each other and the future we all have to share.
I know I have big shoes to fill. In my grandfather's memory, I've led a life of caring about this a lot. I put that care and effort and hope into everything I do.
But this is bigger than me. It's bigger than my family's legacy.
Hope is hard to find in Politics these days, but if we let it die out completely, that's how we really lose. Now cannot be the time to stop caring or turn away. We have to double down in our pursuit of hope.
I really think this election is the one — our last chance to stop Trump and change the direction we're heading in.

| | | | High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.

Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She worked for every inch of ground she’s gained.

Housing has always been personal for me. By high school, my family had been evicted three times. So when I’m able to help Milwaukee families achieve the dream of homeownership, that’s not just good policy – it’s a personal victory.

**Opioid deaths continue to drop county-wide, including a 30% drop in 2024.**

clean_body: What happens in Milwaukee County isn’t just a local success story – it’s a blueprint for what we can accomplish statewide with the right leadership. | | Hi Peter, This morning I had the pleasure of delivering my 2026 State of the County address to a packed crowd of Milwaukee County residents. From catastrophic floods to diminished federal funding, there’s been no shortage of challenges over the past year. But through it all, I’m proud to say that we’ve managed to balance the budget and continue making life better for Milwaukee County residents. What happens in Milwaukee County isn’t just a local success story – it’s a blueprint for what we can accomplish statewide with the right leadership. Here’s a glimpse of what we’ve accomplished: Since taking office, I’ve delivered more than $50 million for affordable housing. That means building in suburbs, cities and everywhere in between. And the results speak for themselves – in 2025, Milwaukee County had the lowest unsheltered population per capita in the entire country. Housing has always been personal for me. By high school, my family had been evicted three times. So when I’m able to help Milwaukee families achieve the dream of homeownership, that’s not just good policy – it’s a personal victory. Opioid deaths continue to drop county-wide, including a 30% drop in 2024. Statistics are still being compiled for 2025, but preliminary data suggests we are on track for another substantial drop. These changes reflect an all-of-the-above solution to our county’s addiction crisis, incorporating behavioral health providers, harm reduction services, and regional partnerships to identify overdose spikes. Our Building Bridges program continues to grow small businesses, leveraging more than $1.8 million in investments and supporting 120+ jobs. Whether it’s revitalizing storefronts, activating commercial corridors, or creating jobs block by block, we’re hard at work growing an economy rooted in local ownership and union labor. I’m running for governor to take this program statewide, because building an economy that works everywhere means making sure small businesses can thrive anywhere. I’ve balanced the budget every single year I’ve been in office, and delivered the largest property tax cut in Milwaukee County history. What’s more, we also ended 2025 with a $14 million surplus – despite drastic cuts from the Trump Administration. By addressing pension issues, creating additional revenue sources, and securing reimbursements for state-mandated services, I’ve led Milwaukee County onto stable economic footing and ensured that we can continue investing in better outcomes for our residents. Hi Peter,

Tonight marks the end of Ramadan and the beginning of Eid al-Fitr — a day
of celebration, gratitude, and community for Muslims around the world.

Ramadan is a time for reflection. A time to slow down, reconnect with
faith, and remember our responsibilities to one another.

It’s also a time that reminds me why I got into public service in the
first place. At its core, Ramadan teaches something simple: We are
responsible for each other.

We’re called to care for the vulnerable, to give generously, and to build
a society rooted in compassion and justice.

Those values shape how I think about politics, too.

In the richest country in the world, it shouldn’t be this hard to afford
healthcare. It shouldn’t be this hard to start and run a successful small
business. And it shouldn’t be this hard for our government to care about
the people it serves.

I believe we can build something better together, and god willing, we
will.

However you’re celebrating, I hope your home is filled with joy, good
food, and the people you love.

From my family to yours, Eid Mubarak!

With gratitude,

Abdul
